Question 47

How many equal /27 subnets can be created from 192.168.20.0/24, counting every subnet?

  • A. 8
  • B. 16
  • C. 32
  • D. 64

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam · 2015 · Question 65

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule.

Study-guide sections

NET26 · Borrow bits and choose a mask

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET26 · Borrow bits and choose a mask

Correct answer: A — 8

Subnet counts depend on both the parent and child prefixes. Dividing a /24 parent into /27 children borrows three bits, giving 2^3 = 8 subnets. Each child has five host bits and therefore 32 total addresses, but that address count is a different quantity. Counting every subnet avoids the obsolete practice of excluding the first and last subnet.

Evidence in the complete study note

To split parent /a into equal /p blocks, borrow b=p-a bits and obtain 2^b subnets. Do not subtract two subnets under modern practice. For a Class B /16 parent split to /19, b=3 gives eight subnets, each with 8192 addresses and 8190 conventional hosts. A /19 alone does not state its parent.NET26
For H hosts, choose the smallest h satisfying 2^h-2≥H, then p=32-h. For 24 hosts use /27; 52 or 57 use /26; 100 use /25; 500 use /23. For at least six equal subnets choose b=3. A Class C /24 split to /27 yields eight subnets. Always check both the number of subnets and the host capacity.NET26

Choice by choice

A · correct — Three borrowed bits produce eight /27 subnets.

B · incorrect — Sixteen would require four borrowed bits, not three.

C · incorrect — Thirty-two is the number of addresses in each /27, not the number of children of this /24.

D · incorrect — Sixty-four requires six borrowed bits rather than three.

Question 48

Given an IP Address 172.16.28.252 with the subnet mask of 255.255.240.0 what is the correct network address?

  • A. 172.16.24.0
  • B. 172.16.28.0
  • C. 172.16.0.0
  • D. 172.16.16.0

Source

  • Computer Science model exam · 2015 · Question 70

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule.

Study-guide sections

NET24 · Masks, prefixes and binary AND

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET24 · Masks, prefixes and binary AND

Correct answer: D — 172.16.16.0

240=11110000 in the third mask octet. 28 (00011100) AND 240 (11110000)=16 (00010000); the last masked octet is zero. Thus the network is 172.16.16.0. Evidence: PDF 18, 19, 19.

Evidence in the complete study note

A /p IPv4 prefix has p leading one bits followed by 32-p zeros. Partial octet masks are 128,192,224,240,248,252,254. /19 is 255.255.224.0; /20 is 255.255.240.0; /21 is 255.255.248.0, correcting the study guide’s 255.248.0.0 mistake.NET24
Compute network=address AND mask. Host bits zero identify the block start; host bits one give broadcast. With 172.16.28.252/20, the third octet is grouped in blocks of 16, so the network is 172.16.16.0 and broadcast 172.16.31.255. A written host/prefix such as 172.105.180.0/21 need not be an aligned block label: masking yields 172.105.176.0/21.NET24

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — 24 is not aligned to a 16-wide third-octet block (PDF 18, 19, 19.)

B · incorrect — 28 retains host bits instead of masking them (PDF 18, 19, 19.)

C · incorrect — 0 would discard the retained third-octet network bit (PDF 18, 19, 19.)

D · correct — 16 is the result of the mask operation (PDF 18, 19, 19.)

Question 49

One of the following is true about packet switching.

  • A. Packets travel around the network seeking out the most efficient route.
  • B. Packets should necessarily seek out the shortest route.
  • C. The message gets broken into small data packets.
  • D. All

Source

  • Computer Science model exam · 2015 · Question 71

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions.

Study-guide sections

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

Correct answer: C — Packet switching divides a message into packets

The defining packet-switching property is dividing data into packets for shared-link forwarding. Routing may seek good paths, but packets do not guarantee the most efficient or geometrically shortest path. C directly states the definition; D includes unsupported universal route claims and therefore fails.

Evidence in the complete study note

Circuit switching sets up a path with reserved resources, transfers data, then releases it. Predictable allocated bandwidth trades against setup/blocking and wasted reservation during silence. A traditional telephone call is the standard example. Packet switching divides data into packets that share links statistically; queueing can add variable delay and loss. This does not make modern voice-over-packet impossible: buffering, scheduling and capacity planning manage it.NET31
Datagram packets are forwarded independently. Virtual circuits establish forwarding state, but resource reservation is optional, not a necessary property of every virtual circuit. Message switching stores a complete message before forwarding, without a dedicated end-to-end path. Packet store-and-forward waits for the full packet/frame; cut-through starts after enough header arrives; fragment-free historically waits through the initial collision-sensitive portion. No routing algorithm guarantees that every packet always takes the geometrically shortest route.NET31

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Routing chooses next hops, but packet switching does not guarantee packets discover the globally most efficient route.

B · incorrect — Packets are not guaranteed to take the geometrically shortest route.

C · correct — Breaking a message into data packets is the packet-switching operation.

D · incorrect — The all option includes unsupported route-optimality and necessary-shortest-path claims.

Question 50

Which statements correctly compare the seven-layer OSI reference model with the four-layer TCP/IP model? Select all that apply.

  • A. Both have application layers.
  • B. Both have comparable transport and network layers.
  • C. Both uses packet-switching instead of circuit-switching technology.
  • D. All

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam · 2015 · Question 72

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.

Study-guide sections

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

NET03 · Protocols, standards and layers

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

NET03 · Protocols, standards and layers

Correct answers (select all): A, B — Both have application layers.; Both have comparable transport and network layers.

Both models include application responsibilities and corresponding transport and network functions. TCP/IP groups the OSI session, presentation and application responsibilities into its application layer, and calls its network layer the Internet layer. An abstract reference model does not itself execute a switching technology. Consequently, the claim that both models necessarily use packet switching is not a valid shared model property.

Evidence in the complete study note

The four-layer TCP/IP model folds OSI layers 5–7 into application, retains transport, calls layer 3 Internet, and combines link/physical as network access. A model is a guide to functions, not a guarantee that every application gets a reliable network. Distinguish end-to-end application service from its underlying process-to-process transport.NET19
A reference model divides responsibilities and interfaces; it is not itself executable networking software. OSI is a seven-layer reference model; TCP/IP describes an implemented protocol suite, usually taught with four layers. A five-layer teaching model separates physical and link functions. State the model before counting layers.NET03

Choice by choice

A · correct — Both models include an application layer, although TCP/IP folds several OSI upper-layer functions into it.

B · correct — TCP/IP retains transport and maps OSI network responsibilities to its Internet layer.

C · incorrect — A reference model does not itself use a switching technology or restrict every implementation to one.

D · incorrect — The implemented-technology claim in C is not a property established for both abstract models.

Question 51

One of the following is network layer protocol.

  • A. HTTP
  • B. FTP
  • C. ARP
  • D. TCP

Source

  • Computer Science model exam · 2015 · Question 73

Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.

NET20 · DNS, DHCP and address resolution

NET21 · Web, file, mail and remote-login protocols

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET20 · DNS, DHCP and address resolution

NET21 · Web, file, mail and remote-login protocols

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Correct answer: C — ARP

Within this module, ARP is grouped among protocols supporting IP at the network layer. This follows the assigned taxonomy rather than assuming that all taxonomies place ARP identically. Evidence: PDF 17, 17, 18, 18.

Evidence in the complete study note

ARP resolves an on-link IPv4 next hop to a link address, using a broadcast request and normally unicast reply. For an off-subnet target, ARP resolves the gateway, not the remote target’s MAC. It bridges the network/link addressing boundary and is often classified at the link layer; calling ARP simply a network protocol uses a loose textbook convention. RARP reverses hardware-to-IP lookup; BOOTP/DHCP support boot configuration. ICMP reports errors and diagnostics; IGMP manages IPv4 multicast membership. These are separate companion protocols, not four pieces whose combination is IP.NET20
HTTP defines web request/response semantics; it is stateless, and a message body may be absent. HTTPS adds TLS protection. FTP transfers files using control and separate data connections; it is not the same protocol as SFTP. SMTP submits and relays mail; POP3 retrieves messages and IMAP accesses/synchronizes server mailboxes. Saying SMTP handles both sending and end-user mailbox retrieval is inaccurate.NET21
TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.NET17

Question 53

Which listed device performs layer-1 signal regeneration without inspecting destination addresses?

  • A. Router
  • B. Switch
  • C. Firewall
  • D. Repeater

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam · 2015 · Question 105

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.

Study-guide sections

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

NET11 · Routers, gateways and traffic controls

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

NET11 · Routers, gateways and traffic controls

Correct answer: D — Repeater

A repeater regenerates physical signals and therefore performs a layer-1 function. Routers decide where to forward network-layer packets, and ordinary Ethernet switches make link-layer decisions using MAC addresses. A firewall enforces a security policy rather than defining a physical signal-regeneration role. Replacing the duplicated firewall distractor restores a meaningful physical-layer choice without changing the layer-identification concept.

Evidence in the complete study note

A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.NET09
A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.NET10
A firewall allows, rejects or inspects traffic under a security policy; it does not necessarily encrypt. A VPN, Virtual Private Network, provides a logical private connection over another network; a secure VPN authenticates/encrypts its tunnel. A modem modulates outgoing and demodulates incoming carrier signals. These functions may coexist in one home router but remain conceptually distinct.NET11

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — A router’s defining forwarding function is network-layer IP routing rather than layer-1 signal repetition.

B · incorrect — An ordinary Ethernet switch performs layer-2 MAC frame forwarding.

C · incorrect — A firewall enforces traffic policy rather than being the layer-1 repeater/hub requested.

D · correct — A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses.

As a syntactic IPv4 address comparison, 257 exceeds the permitted 0-255 octet range. The others have four legal octets; no host mask is supplied to test host assignability. Evidence: PDF 19.

Evidence in the complete study note

Write IPv4 as four decimal octets 0–255, or as 32 binary bits. Use weights 128,64,32,16,8,4,2,1 within each octet. Thus 11000001 10000011 00011011 11111111 is 193.131.27.255. A value such as 257 is impossible. Syntactic validity differs from assignability: an address ending .0 or .255 can be a host under some prefixes.NET22

Choice by choice

A · correct — 257 violates the octet limit (PDF 19.)

B · incorrect — All octets fall between 0 and 255 (PDF 19.)

C · incorrect — All octets fall between 0 and 255 (PDF 19.)

D · incorrect — All octets fall between 0 and 255 (PDF 19.)

Question 57

The most commonly used method to convert analog data to digital form.

  • A. Line coding scheme
  • B. Data encoding
  • C. Pulse code modulation
  • D. Demodulation

Source

  • Computer Science model exam · 2015 · Question 109

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule.

Study-guide sections

NET15 · Line coding, modulation and sampling

NET11 · Routers, gateways and traffic controls

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET15 · Line coding, modulation and sampling

NET11 · Routers, gateways and traffic controls

Correct answer: C — Pulse code modulation (PCM)

NET15 identifies PCM as the analog-to-digital procedure of sampling the analog input, quantizing each sample and encoding its level as bits. The note does not establish comparative usage statistics, but PCM is the specific conversion method among the choices. Line coding maps existing digital bits to signals; demodulation recovers information from a carrier rather than necessarily digitizing analog data.

Evidence in the complete study note

ASK varies carrier amplitude, FSK frequency, PSK phase; QAM combines amplitude and phase. AM/FM/PM can carry analog data. PCM digitizes analog input by sampling, quantizing and encoding. Sampling must exceed twice the highest retained baseband frequency in practical designs; b-bit samples have 2^b quantization levels and uncompressed rate fs×b. PAM/PWM are pulse modulation methods; pulse amplitude or width alone is not a binary PCM code.NET15
Line coding maps digital bits to digital signal patterns. NRZ uses levels without a forced mid-bit return; Manchester supplies a mid-bit transition for clocking, with bit convention specified. Differential Manchester encodes using transitions relative to previous state. AMI alternates the polarity of successive ones; pseudoternary alternates zero pulses. Block coding adds code redundancy; scrambling replaces problematic patterns without necessarily increasing bit count. Multilevel schemes include 2B1Q and 8B6T; MLT-3 uses a sequence of voltage transitions.NET15
A firewall allows, rejects or inspects traffic under a security policy; it does not necessarily encrypt. A VPN, Virtual Private Network, provides a logical private connection over another network; a secure VPN authenticates/encrypts its tunnel. A modem modulates outgoing and demodulates incoming carrier signals. These functions may coexist in one home router but remain conceptually distinct.NET11

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Line coding begins with digital bits and maps them to digital signal patterns, rather than digitizing analog input.

B · incorrect — Data encoding is a broad description and does not identify the specific analog-digitization method supplied here.

C · correct — PCM performs the sampling, quantization and binary encoding needed to turn analog input into digital data.

D · incorrect — Demodulation removes carrier modulation; it does not itself specify analog-to-digital sampling and quantization.

Question 58

In a peer-to-peer architecture, which statements are false? Select all that apply. Interpret C as absence of a required client-server hierarchy.

  • A. Computers can function as both a client and a server.
  • B. A dedicated central administrator is required by peer-to-peer architecture.
  • C. There is no a hierarchy among the computers.
  • D. In peer - to - peer network security is not an issue.

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam · 2015 · Question 116

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule.

Study-guide sections

NET02 · Network size, access and architecture

NET33 · Identify networking layers and addressing assumptions

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET02 · Network size, access and architecture

NET33 · Identify networking layers and addressing assumptions

Correct answers (select all): B, D — A dedicated central administrator is required by peer-to-peer architecture.; In peer - to - peer network security is not an issue.

Peers may request and supply services without a required client-server hierarchy. That capability does not impose a dedicated central administrator, although people may still take responsibility for administration. Peer systems also continue to need security because they expose data and services. The false statements therefore concern mandatory centralized administration and the dismissal of security, while the capability and no-required-hierarchy statements are true.

Evidence in the complete study note

An intranet serves an organization internally; an extranet exposes selected services to approved outsiders. Neither term alone specifies geographic size. A client requests a service; a server supplies it. Peer systems may perform both roles. Dedicated servers concentrate on service workloads but can still be clients of DNS, backup or update services. A ten-user cutoff is a teaching guideline, not a technical law. Centralization simplifies administration but creates dependencies; peer networks still need security.NET02
First identify the exact layer, protocol and scope. Flow/error control can exist at both link and transport layers; MAC addresses can be locally administered; bridges and switches both operate at layer 2. A LAN can use public or private unicast space. UDP and IP are both connectionless. Session dialogs and TCP connections are distinct senses of connection. Distinguish the protocol, layer and scope before treating these descriptions as exclusive.NET33

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — True: peers can both request and supply services, so this is not a false statement.

B · correct — False: a dedicated central administrator is not a requirement of peer architecture.

C · incorrect — True: peers do not require a client-server hierarchy, so this is not a false statement.

D · correct — False: peer networks still require security.

Question 60

Which single option gives the complete set of listed devices whose ordinary forwarding function is at the data-link layer?

  • A. Switch
  • B. Access point
  • C. Hub
  • D. A & B

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam · 2015 · Question 123

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.

Study-guide sections

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

Correct answer: D — A & B

An ordinary Ethernet switch forwards frames at layer 2, and an ordinary wireless access point bridges wireless and wired link-layer traffic. A hub simply repeats physical signals at layer 1. The question requests the complete set, so either switch or access point alone omits another qualifying device. The combined response is therefore the one complete selection.

Evidence in the complete study note

A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.NET10
A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.NET09

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — A switch is layer 2, but this selection omits the qualifying access point.

B · incorrect — A bridging access point is layer 2, but this selection omits the switch.

C · incorrect — A hub repeats physical signals and does not inspect destination MAC addresses as a data-link device does.

D · correct — Both the ordinary switch and bridging access point are data-link devices; this gives the complete set.

Question 61

Which statement correctly describes the OSI reference model?

  • A. It has fewer layer that TCP/IP model.
  • B. The model itself is executable software installed to implement a network.
  • C. Used as a guide to help students or learners understand the communication process.
  • D. All

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam · 2015 · Question 125

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.

Study-guide sections

NET03 · Protocols, standards and layers

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET03 · Protocols, standards and layers

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

Correct answer: C — Used as a guide to help students or learners understand the communication process.

OSI divides communication responsibilities into seven layers and serves as a framework for explaining interfaces and communication processes. The usual TCP/IP teaching model has four layers, so OSI does not have fewer. A reference model can guide design, but it is not itself executable networking software or an installed protocol implementation. That distinction makes the learning-guide statement the correct description.

Evidence in the complete study note

A reference model divides responsibilities and interfaces; it is not itself executable networking software. OSI is a seven-layer reference model; TCP/IP describes an implemented protocol suite, usually taught with four layers. A five-layer teaching model separates physical and link functions. State the model before counting layers.NET03
The four-layer TCP/IP model folds OSI layers 5–7 into application, retains transport, calls layer 3 Internet, and combines link/physical as network access. A model is a guide to functions, not a guarantee that every application gets a reliable network. Distinguish end-to-end application service from its underlying process-to-process transport.NET19

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — OSI has seven layers, more than the usual four-layer TCP/IP teaching model.

B · incorrect — A reference model is not itself executable networking software, although it can guide design.

C · correct — The model helps learners understand layered communication responsibilities.

D · incorrect — The incorrect layer count and executable-software claim prevent all statements from being true.

  • C. Sender

  • Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 40

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule.

Study-guide sections

NET01 · Communication components and quality

NET06 · Delay, impairments and transmission modes

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET01 · Communication components and quality

NET06 · Delay, impairments and transmission modes

Correct answer: D — Distance

The five basic components are message, sender, receiver, medium and protocol. Message, medium and sender therefore belong to the required set. Distance affects transmission engineering, such as propagation delay and attenuation, but it is not a sixth component in that model. Replacing the original protocol option with distance supplies a meaningful exception while retaining the negative component-identification task.

Evidence in the complete study note

Data are raw representations; information is data interpreted for a purpose. Communication requires a message, sender, receiver, medium and agreed protocol. A source creates data; a transmitter converts it to a signal; a receiver reconstructs data. Distance affects engineering but is not a sixth component.NET01
Transmission delay is packet bits divided by link bit rate; propagation delay is distance divided by signal speed. Processing and queueing add delay. A 1000-byte packet takes 0.8 ms to serialize at 10 Mbit/s; increasing line rate does not reduce propagation time.NET06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Message is explicitly one of the required components.

B · incorrect — The medium carries signals and is explicitly a communication component.

C · incorrect — The sender is explicitly included among communication components.

D · correct — Distance affects engineering but is not one of the five basic communication components.

Question 63

There are two types of network topologies from these topologies which one of the following defines how hosts access the media to send data.

  • B. Bus Topology
  • C. Physical Topology
  • D. Star Topology

  • Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 41

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Study-guide sections

NET08 · Topology and failure reasoning

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET08 · Topology and failure reasoning

Correct answer: A — Logical topology

The distinction is between physical layout and communication/access relationships. NET08 defines logical topology in the latter sense, matching how hosts obtain medium access. Bus and star are particular arrangements rather than the general physical-versus-logical category requested.

Evidence in the complete study note

Physical topology describes link layout; logical topology describes communication/access relationships. Point-to-point links join two endpoints; multipoint links share a medium. A full mesh consists of point-to-point links.NET08
Bus uses a shared backbone; an unterminated break can disrupt the segment. Star connects endpoints through a central device: one edge failure isolates that endpoint, whereas central failure affects the star. Ring forms a loop; basic single rings are vulnerable to a break, while protected dual rings differ. Token passing is associated with Token Ring but is an access method, not a necessary property of every ring. Tree is hierarchical; hybrid combines arrangements.NET08

A · correct — Logical topology describes communication and medium-access relationships among hosts.

B · incorrect — Bus is a particular shared-backbone arrangement, not the general category defining access relationships.

C · incorrect — Physical topology describes link layout and connections rather than the logical rules for medium access.

D · incorrect — Star describes endpoints around a central device; it does not name the general access-topology category.

Question 64

  • B. Data Link
  • C. Network
  • D. Transport

  • Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 42

Study-guide sections

NET12 · OSI layers and encapsulation

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET12 · OSI layers and encapsulation

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Correct answer: D — Transport

Transport explicitly divides data into segments and reassembles sequence-numbered segments. Evidence: PDF 16, 14, 15, 15.

Evidence in the complete study note

Sending proceeds from application data to transport segment/datagram, network packet, link frame and physical bits/symbols; receiving reverses the order. Each layer serves the layer above. A router removes a received link frame, inspects IP, and creates a new link frame for the next hop. MAC addresses usually change across routed hops; end-to-end IP addresses ordinarily remain until translation.NET12
TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.NET17

B · incorrect — Data link handles frames (PDF 16, 14, 15, 15.)

Question 66

You want to implement a network medium that is not susceptible to EMI. Which type of cabling should you use?

  • A. Coaxial
  • B. Category 6 UTP
  • C. Microwave
  • D. Fiber-optic

Source

  • Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 44

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Compare the signal mechanism, medium properties or transmission direction against the definitions and stated physical assumptions.

Study-guide sections

NET07 · Cables, wireless and connectors

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET07 · Cables, wireless and connectors

Correct answer: D — Fiber-optic cable

NET07 identifies fiber as a light-guiding medium that resists electromagnetic interference. Coax and UTP carry electrical signals and can be affected by coupled interference. Microwave is wireless, so it is not a cabling answer even before considering interference in radio transmission.

Evidence in the complete study note

Twisted pairs reduce coupled interference; UTP has no added shield and STP adds shielding. Coax has an inner conductor and outer shield sharing an axis. Fiber guides light and resists electromagnetic interference; it supports high capacity and long reach, but requires suitable optics and installation. Exact speed, cost and reach depend on the specification, not the material alone. Fiber can still be tapped.NET07
Radio, microwave and infrared are unguided media. Ground waves follow Earth, sky waves can reflect from ionized layers, and line-of-sight paths require suitable visibility. Microwaves are radio waves in the broader physical classification. Infrared generally does not penetrate walls. Directionality depends on antennas: omnidirectional means broad azimuth coverage, not equal radiation in every 3-D direction. Legacy Ethernet straight-through cables join unlike MDI/MDI-X roles; crossover joins like roles, such as PC–PC or switch–switch. Auto-MDI-X can remove that requirement.NET07

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Coax has shielding but still carries electrical signals; it does not offer fiber’s immunity to electromagnetic coupling.

B · incorrect — Twisted pairs reduce interference but unshielded copper cable remains susceptible to electromagnetic coupling.

C · incorrect — Microwave is an unguided wireless medium, not a cable matching the requested cabling choice.

D · correct — Fiber carries light and resists electromagnetic interference rather than conducting the unwanted electrical coupling.

NET13 · Link control, framing and error detection

Logical network addressing, such as IP addressing, supports delivery across interconnected networks and belongs to the network layer. The data-link layer instead handles local frame delivery, hardware/MAC addressing, medium access and link-control functions. LLC identifies or multiplexes upper-layer protocols and may supply link control. The term hardware addressing here denotes frame-level MAC addressing, not an IP address.

Link-layer LLC identifies or multiplexes upper-layer protocols and may supply link control; MAC handles medium-dependent addressing/access and frame delivery. Network addressing belongs to layer 3. Ethernet, PPP and HDLC are link protocols. Frame headers may carry addresses and control/type fields; synchronization and exact framing depend on the protocol.NET13

Question 68

Which class of IP address provides a maximum of only 254 host addresses per network ID?

  • A. Class A
  • B. Class D
  • C. Class B
  • D. Class C

Source

  • Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 46

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule.

Study-guide sections

NET22 · IPv4 notation and classful defaults

NET25 · Find subnet bounds and usable hosts

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET22 · IPv4 notation and classful defaults

NET25 · Find subnet bounds and usable hosts

Correct answer: D — Class C under the historical default mask

The wording asks about historical address classes. Class C uses default /24, leaving eight host bits: 2^8−2=254 ordinary usable hosts. Classes A and B leave more bits, while Class D identifies multicast rather than an ordinary unicast host network. Under CIDR the actual prefix would replace these defaults.

Evidence in the complete study note

Historical classes use leading patterns: A 0 with /8, B 10 with /16, C 110 with /24; D 1110 is multicast and E 1111 reserved. Ordinary class-A first octets are 1–126 because 0 and 127 have special uses. B spans 128–191 and C 192–223. Default usable counts are 2^24-2, 2^16-2 and 254. Modern CIDR requires the actual prefix and overrides class defaults.NET22
For ordinary broadcast LANs let h=32-p. Total addresses=2^h; usable hosts=2^h-2, reserving network and directed broadcast. Find the changing octet’s increment as 256-mask octet, round the address down to a multiple, and extend through the next boundary minus one.NET25

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Default Class A /8 leaves 24 host bits, far more than 254 usable hosts.

B · incorrect — Class D is multicast space, not an ordinary classful unicast network with 254 hosts.

C · incorrect — Default Class B /16 leaves sixteen host bits and 65534 ordinary usable hosts.

D · correct — Default Class C /24 leaves eight host bits, giving 256 addresses minus network and broadcast.

A sine wave has amplitude, frequency and phase. Given propagation speed, wavelength follows from frequency and describes its spatial repetition. Analog signals vary continuously; digital signals use discrete symbol states. Data and signal types are separate: digital bits can modulate an analog carrier. A sine wave has amplitude, frequency and phase. Frequency f counts cycles/second, period T=1/f, and wavelength λ=v/f depends on propagation speed v. Phase specifies displacement within a cycle. Composite signals combine frequencies.NET04
Line coding maps digital bits to digital signal patterns. NRZ uses levels without a forced mid-bit return; Manchester supplies a mid-bit transition for clocking, with bit convention specified. Differential Manchester encodes using transitions relative to previous state. AMI alternates the polarity of successive ones; pseudoternary alternates zero pulses. Block coding adds code redundancy; scrambling replaces problematic patterns without necessarily increasing bit count. Multilevel schemes include 2B1Q and 8B6T; MLT-3 uses a sequence of voltage transitions.NET15

Routers forward IP packets between networks and separate broadcast domains. Packet filtering can accompany the traffic-control function, so A is the normal-function exception, not a claim that no specially configured broadcast relay can exist.

A default gateway is usually a router, while a protocol gateway can translate application formats; therefore a gateway is not inherently a device that implements every OSI layer.NET11
A firewall allows, rejects or inspects traffic under a security policy; it does not necessarily encrypt. A modem modulates outgoing and demodulates incoming carrier signals. These functions may coexist in one home router but remain conceptually distinct.NET11

Question 72

Which OSI layer uses acknowledgments, sequencing and receiver flow control for end-to-end process delivery, as illustrated by TCP?

  • A. Layer 2
  • B. Layer 4
  • C. Layer 3
  • D. Layer 7

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 50

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.

Study-guide sections

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Correct answer: B — Layer 4

Scope separates otherwise similar mechanisms. Reliable link procedures can acknowledge frames and control a single hop, whereas TCP uses sequence numbers, acknowledgments and windows between transport endpoints. The explicit end-to-end process-delivery requirement identifies layer 4. IP at layer 3 offers best-effort delivery, and application services build on the transport service rather than defining this TCP reliability machinery.

Evidence in the complete study note

Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.NET14
TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.NET17

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Layer 2 can provide similar mechanisms only for hop-local link delivery, outside the requested scope.

B · correct — Layer 4 transport provides TCP’s end-to-end sequencing, acknowledgments and receiver flow control.

C · incorrect — IP best-effort delivery does not provide the indicated ordered acknowledgment/retransmission service.

D · incorrect — Application services can build reliability, but the standard link/transport mechanisms named here are not layer-7 duties.

Question 73

What is the technique of combining multiple input signals or streams onto a shared transmission link?

  • A. Broadcast
  • B. Multicast
  • C. Multiplexing
  • D. demultiplexing

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 51

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Compare the signal mechanism, medium properties or transmission direction against the definitions and stated physical assumptions.

Study-guide sections

NET32 · Multiplexing and channelization

NET30 · Routing algorithms and destination sets

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET32 · Multiplexing and channelization

NET30 · Routing algorithms and destination sets

Correct answer: C — Multiplexing

Multiplexing combines input signals or streams so they share a link, using distinctions such as frequency, wavelength or time slots. Demultiplexing is the corresponding receiver operation that separates them. Broadcast and multicast instead describe recipient sets for a message. Link sharing and destination distribution therefore answer different questions, even though a network can use both mechanisms.

Evidence in the complete study note

Multiplexing combines multiple input streams onto a shared link; demultiplexing separates them at the receiver. It differs from broadcasting one message to many destinations. FDM assigns distinct frequency bands with suitable guard spacing; WDM assigns different optical wavelengths. TDM allocates time slots: synchronous TDM reserves recurrent slots even if an input is idle, while statistical TDM allocates according to demand and needs identification.NET32
Flooding sends copies on eligible outgoing links with duplicate/lifetime controls; random walk picks a neighbor probabilistically. Unicast targets one destination, broadcast all in a scope, multicast a subscribed group and anycast one member sharing an address, normally nearest under routing metrics. Multi-destination packets can list multiple targets; this is not necessarily identical to broadcast. Group multicast trees use mechanisms such as reverse-path checks; Ethernet spanning tree is a different layer-2 mechanism.NET30

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Broadcast distributes a message to all members of a broadcast domain rather than combining input streams.

B · incorrect — Multicast distributes to a receiver group rather than combining inputs onto a link.

C · correct — Multiplexing combines inputs onto the shared link.

D · incorrect — Demultiplexing separates received multiplexed inputs; it is the reverse operation.

Correct answer: D — Class B

Two octets are sixteen bits. A historical Class B default /16 therefore uses the first two octets as network bits and the final two as host bits. Class A defaults to one network octet and Class C to three; Class D is multicast. Actual CIDR allocation can override the historical defaults.

Historical classes use leading patterns: A 0 with /8, B 10 with /16, C 110 with /24; D 1110 is multicast and E 1111 reserved. A /p IPv4 prefix has p leading one bits followed by 32-p zeros. Partial octet masks are 128,192,224,240,248,252,254. /19 is 255.255.224.0; /20 is 255.255.240.0; /21 is 255.255.248.0, correcting the study guide’s 255.248.0.0 mistake.NET24

D · correct — Class B defaults to /16, exactly the two-network-octet, two-host-octet division described.

Question 81

Which one of the following is disadvantage of circuit switching?

  • A. Predictable performance
  • B. Low latency
  • C. Guaranteed bandwidth
  • D. Limited scalability

Source

  • Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 92

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Study-guide sections

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

Correct answer: D — Limited scalability due to reserved resources

Circuit switching reserves resources for an established path. NET31 explains that this offers predictable bandwidth but introduces setup, blocking and unused reservation during silence. Those costs constrain how many simultaneous circuits can be supported as demand grows, making limited scalability the disadvantage among the offered choices.

Evidence in the complete study note

Circuit switching sets up a path with reserved resources, transfers data, then releases it. Predictable allocated bandwidth trades against setup/blocking and wasted reservation during silence. A traditional telephone call is the standard example. Packet switching divides data into packets that share links statistically; queueing can add variable delay and loss. This does not make modern voice-over-packet impossible: buffering, scheduling and capacity planning manage it.NET31

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Predictable performance is a benefit of allocated circuit resources, not the disadvantage requested.

B · incorrect — Low transfer latency after setup can be beneficial; the relevant costs include setup and resource reservation.

C · incorrect — Guaranteed allocated bandwidth is an advantage, although reserving it consumes capacity during silence.

D · correct — Finite reserved resources and blocking constrain simultaneous connections and therefore scalability as demand grows.

Question 82

Study-guide sections

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

Correct answer: A — Circuit switching

A dedicated path is explicitly required by circuit switching. Packet communication is contrasted with that continuous dedicated circuit.

Evidence in the complete study note

Circuit switching sets up a path with reserved resources, transfers data, then releases it. Predictable allocated bandwidth trades against setup/blocking and wasted reservation during silence. A traditional telephone call is the standard example. Packet switching divides data into packets that share links statistically; queueing can add variable delay and loss. This does not make modern voice-over-packet impossible: buffering, scheduling and capacity planning manage it.NET31
Datagram packets are forwarded independently. Virtual circuits establish forwarding state, but resource reservation is optional, not a necessary property of every virtual circuit. Message switching stores a complete message before forwarding, without a dedicated end-to-end path. Packet store-and-forward waits for the full packet/frame; cut-through starts after enough header arrives; fragment-free historically waits through the initial collision-sensitive portion. No routing algorithm guarantees that every packet always takes the geometrically shortest route.NET31

B · incorrect — Packet communication is discrete rather than the dedicated circuit

C · incorrect — Both incorrectly adds a requirement not inherent to packet switching

Question 85

Which one of the data communication mediums is used for direct transmission?

  • A. Induced
  • B. Crosstalk
  • C. A and B
  • D. None of the above

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET07 · Cables, wireless and connectors

NET06 · Delay, impairments and transmission modes

Correct answer: D — Neither induced nor crosstalk names a transmission medium

The note identifies cables and unguided radio/microwave/infrared as transmission media. Crosstalk instead names interference from nearby channels in NET06, and induced alone does not name a medium in the note. Regardless of the vague direct-transmission phrase, none of A–C supplies a listed medium, so D is the supported exclusion response.

Evidence in the complete study note

Radio, microwave and infrared are unguided media. Ground waves follow Earth, sky waves can reflect from ionized layers, and line-of-sight paths require suitable visibility. Microwaves are radio waves in the broader physical classification. Infrared generally does not penetrate walls. Directionality depends on antennas: omnidirectional means broad azimuth coverage, not equal radiation in every 3-D direction. Legacy Ethernet straight-through cables join unlike MDI/MDI-X roles; crossover joins like roles, such as PC–PC or switch–switch. Auto-MDI-X can remove that requirement.NET07
Attenuation reduces signal strength. Distortion changes shape, often because frequencies have different delays. Noise adds unwanted energy: thermal noise comes from random thermal motion, crosstalk leaks from nearby channels, and impulse noise is a short disturbance. Amplifiers amplify noise too; digital repeaters regenerate decisions but cannot reconstruct every corrupted bit.NET06

B · incorrect — Crosstalk is unwanted coupling/interference, not a medium for intentional direct transmission.

C · incorrect — Combining two nonmedium terms does not supply the requested transmission medium.

D · correct — Neither induced nor crosstalk names a transmission medium among the choices.

NET19 distinguishes reducing representation size from hiding content. Compression targets the amount of data needed to represent information, while encryption provides concealment and routing selects paths. Therefore minimizing size is the compression goal; combining it with security and path selection in the all option misattributes unrelated functions.

Evidence in the complete study note

OSI session roles establish/manage dialogs and can coordinate checkpoints so transfer resumes after interruption. Presentation roles translate encodings and handle compression/encryption. Compression reduces representation size; encryption hides content and need not shrink it. Application protocols provide services directly to applications. Practical implementations distribute these functions differently; TLS is not proof of a separate physical presentation-layer device.NET19
Routing computes paths; forwarding chooses a next hop for an individual packet. Select the matching route with the longest prefix, then apply the routing system’s tie-breaking criteria. A default /0 matches when nothing more specific does. Static routes are configured; dynamic protocols exchange reachability. Distance vector uses neighbor estimates, while link state distributes link information and computes shortest paths. Interior protocols operate within an autonomous system; BGP exchanges routes between systems.NET30

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Securing or concealing content is an encryption/security function, not the primary goal of compression.

B · correct — Compression reduces representation size, directly matching minimization of data size.

C · incorrect — Path selection belongs to routing rather than the representation-size transformation performed by compression.

D · incorrect — Only size reduction describes compression here; security and route selection are separate functions.

NET21 · Web, file, mail and remote-login protocols

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET21 · Web, file, mail and remote-login protocols

Correct answer: D — Both POP3 and IMAP

POP3 retrieves stored messages, while IMAP accesses and synchronizes mailboxes held on the server. SMTP instead submits and relays messages between mail-system components. Since the question asks for the complete set of mailbox-access protocols, either POP3 or IMAP alone is incomplete. The combined choice correctly includes both without assigning mailbox retrieval to the mail transfer protocol.

Evidence in the complete study note

HTTP defines web request/response semantics; it is stateless, and a message body may be absent. HTTPS adds TLS protection. FTP transfers files using control and separate data connections; it is not the same protocol as SFTP. SMTP submits and relays mail; POP3 retrieves messages and IMAP accesses/synchronizes server mailboxes. Saying SMTP handles both sending and end-user mailbox retrieval is inaccurate.NET21

B · incorrect — IMAP accesses mailboxes but alone omits POP3, so it is incomplete.

D · correct — Both POP3 and IMAP provide the requested mailbox-access functions.

Question 91

What is the maximum number of IP addresses that can be assigned to hosts on a local subnet that uses the 255.255.255.224 subnet mask?

  • A. 14
  • B. 32
  • C. 24
  • D. 30

Source

  • Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 79

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule.

Study-guide sections

NET25 · Find subnet bounds and usable hosts

NET24 · Masks, prefixes and binary AND

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET25 · Find subnet bounds and usable hosts

NET24 · Masks, prefixes and binary AND

Correct answer: D — 30 usable host addresses

The final mask octet 224 is 11100000, making the prefix /27 and leaving five host bits. There are 2^5=32 addresses in each block. For an ordinary broadcast subnet, one identifies the network and one the broadcast, leaving 30 assignable host addresses; total addresses must not be confused with usable hosts.

Evidence in the complete study note

For ordinary broadcast LANs let h=32-p. Total addresses=2^h; usable hosts=2^h-2, reserving network and directed broadcast. Find the changing octet’s increment as 256-mask octet, round the address down to a multiple, and extend through the next boundary minus one.NET25
A /p IPv4 prefix has p leading one bits followed by 32-p zeros. Partial octet masks are 128,192,224,240,248,252,254. /19 is 255.255.224.0; /20 is 255.255.240.0; /21 is 255.255.248.0, correcting the study guide’s 255.248.0.0 mistake.NET24

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Fourteen usable hosts would correspond to /28, not this /27 mask.

B · incorrect — Thirty-two is the total address count before reserving the network and broadcast addresses.

C · incorrect — Twenty-four is not the usable count obtained from five host bits and two reservations.

D · correct — Five host bits yield 32 total addresses minus two reserved addresses, leaving 30 hosts.

Question 93

Which internet layer address is responsible for providing diagnostic functions and reporting errors or conditions regarding the delivery of IP packets?

  • A. Internet Protocol (IP)
  • B. Address Resolution Protocol (ARP)
  • C. Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP)
  • D. Internet Group Message Protocol (IGMP)

NET16 · Network delivery and IPv4 header

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET20 · DNS, DHCP and address resolution

NET16 · Network delivery and IPv4 header

Correct answer: C — Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP)

ICMP reports transit problems and supports destination-unreachable, echo and timeout diagnostics. The stem calls it an address, but asks for a protocol by its functions. Evidence: PDF 17, 27, 17, 17.

Evidence in the complete study note

ARP resolves an on-link IPv4 next hop to a link address, using a broadcast request and normally unicast reply. For an off-subnet target, ARP resolves the gateway, not the remote target’s MAC. It bridges the network/link addressing boundary and is often classified at the link layer; calling ARP simply a network protocol uses a loose textbook convention. RARP reverses hardware-to-IP lookup; BOOTP/DHCP support boot configuration. ICMP reports errors and diagnostics; IGMP manages IPv4 multicast membership. These are separate companion protocols, not four pieces whose combination is IP.NET20
IP supplies connectionless best-effort packet delivery, not end-to-end ordering or retransmission. IPv4 addresses are 32 bits. Its minimum header is 20 bytes and can grow to 60 bytes; it is not a 32-bit header. IHL counts 32-bit words; total length includes header and payload. TTL limits lifetime across routers; the protocol field identifies TCP, UDP or another upper-layer protocol.NET16

Choice by choice

B · incorrect — ARP resolves IP to hardware address (PDF 17, 27, 17, 17.)

C · correct — ICMP explicitly provides error/diagnostic messages (PDF 17, 27, 17, 17.)

D · incorrect — IGMP supports group recipients rather than these transit diagnostics (PDF 17, 27, 17, 17.)

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET26 · Borrow bits and choose a mask

NET25 · Find subnet bounds and usable hosts

Correct answer: B — 8 subnets and 8190 usable hosts in each subnet

The /16-to-/19 subdivision borrows three bits, so it creates eight equal subnets. Each /19 leaves thirteen host bits, producing 8192 total addresses and 8190 usable hosts after network and broadcast reservations. Modern counting includes every subnet. The option changes only the obsolete subnet count; the calculation still requires distinguishing child subnet count from host capacity.

Evidence in the complete study note

To split parent /a into equal /p blocks, borrow b=p-a bits and obtain 2^b subnets. Do not subtract two subnets under modern practice. For a Class B /16 parent split to /19, b=3 gives eight subnets, each with 8192 addresses and 8190 conventional hosts. A /19 alone does not state its parent.NET26
For ordinary broadcast LANs let h=32-p. Total addresses=2^h; usable hosts=2^h-2, reserving network and directed broadcast. Find the changing octet’s increment as 256-mask octet, round the address down to a multiple, and extend through the next boundary minus one.NET25

A · incorrect — Neither seven subnets nor thirty usable hosts follows from /19; thirty hosts would require /27.

B · correct — Three subnet bits give eight subnets and thirteen host bits give 8190 usable hosts.

C · incorrect — Eight subnets is correct for the stated /16 parent, but a /19 has 8190 usable hosts rather than 2046.

D · incorrect — Seven lacks a stated counting basis, and 2046 hosts corresponds to /21 rather than /19.

Question 95

A switch-based LAN is more efficient than a hub-based LAN because:

  • A. A switch can connect two different LANs together
  • B. A switch allows multiple computers to send at the same time
  • C. A hub uses reservation-based MAC protocols
  • D. A switch uses contention-based MAC protocols
  • E. A switch is easier to implement than a hub.

Source

  • Mock exam 1 · Question 10

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions.

Study-guide sections

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

Correct answer: B — A switch allows multiple computers to send at the same time

Switches direct frames toward the MAC recipient instead of copying all traffic to every port. Independent point-to-point communication permits multiple simultaneous exchanges on suitable separate ports. Evidence: PDF 12, 12.

Evidence in the complete study note

A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.NET10
Each switch port separates collision domains; full-duplex point-to-point Ethernet has no collisions and does not use CSMA/CD. Switching permits independent conversations simultaneously. Broadcasts still reach the VLAN unless another control filters them. A layer-3 switch also routes, so device marketing names do not override the function being examined.NET10
A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.NET09

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Connecting LANs is not the efficiency distinction in the switch/hub comparison (PDF 12, 12.)

B · correct — Selective independent port communication explains the improvement (PDF 12, 12.)

C · incorrect — The module says hubs repeat/broadcast, not reservation-based MAC (PDF 12, 12.)

D · incorrect — A switch is not defined by a contention-based MAC distinction from hubs (PDF 12, 12.)

E · incorrect — The module calls switches more intelligent and expensive, not easier to implement (PDF 12, 12.)

Question 96

Compare circuit switching versus datagram packet switching. An advantage of circuit switching is it:

  • A. Allows end hosts to use different line rates.
  • B. Can guarantee the performance delivered to end hosts.
  • C. Establishes a connection before sending data.
  • D. Sends packets instead of signals.
  • E. Is non-blocking.
  • F. Is efficient when the amount of traffic to be sent by end hosts varies over time.

Source

  • Mock exam 1 · Question 12

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions.

Study-guide sections

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

Correct answer: B — Reserved resources can guarantee performance

The reserved-resource circuit supports predictable allocated bandwidth and performance, the advantage contrasted with datagram links shared statistically. Establishing a connection is a procedural characteristic and imposes setup cost rather than itself guaranteeing a benefit. The note explicitly identifies blocking and wasted reservation during silence, ruling out the nonblocking and variable-traffic-efficiency claims.

Evidence in the complete study note

Circuit switching sets up a path with reserved resources, transfers data, then releases it. Predictable allocated bandwidth trades against setup/blocking and wasted reservation during silence. A traditional telephone call is the standard example. Packet switching divides data into packets that share links statistically; queueing can add variable delay and loss. This does not make modern voice-over-packet impossible: buffering, scheduling and capacity planning manage it.NET31
Datagram packets are forwarded independently. Virtual circuits establish forwarding state, but resource reservation is optional, not a necessary property of every virtual circuit. Message switching stores a complete message before forwarding, without a dedicated end-to-end path. Packet store-and-forward waits for the full packet/frame; cut-through starts after enough header arrives; fragment-free historically waits through the initial collision-sensitive portion. No routing algorithm guarantees that every packet always takes the geometrically shortest route.NET31

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Different endpoint line rates are not the reserved-circuit advantage established in the note.

B · correct — Reserved resources provide predictable allocated bandwidth and can guarantee the agreed performance to endpoints.

C · incorrect — Setup is a characteristic of circuit operation, but is not itself the performance advantage requested.

D · incorrect — Circuit switching establishes reserved resources; packet-versus-signal wording does not describe its advantage.

E · incorrect — NET31 explicitly identifies blocking as a circuit-switching tradeoff.

F · incorrect — Reservations can be wasted during silence, making highly variable traffic less efficient on fixed circuits.

NET08 · Topology and failure reasoning

Correct answer: B — topology

Topology is explicitly the shape/layout and relation among links and devices, matching the way nodes are linked. Evidence: PDF 22, 11.

Evidence in the complete study note

Physical topology describes link layout; logical topology describes communication/access relationships. Point-to-point links join two endpoints; multipoint links share a medium. A full mesh consists of point-to-point links.NET08
Bus uses a shared backbone; an unterminated break can disrupt the segment. Star connects endpoints through a central device: one edge failure isolates that endpoint, whereas central failure affects the star. Token passing is associated with Token Ring but is an access method, not a necessary property of every ring. Tree is hierarchical; hybrid combines arrangements.NET08

Question 100

A topology that involves Tokens.

  • A. Star
  • B. Bus
  • C. Ring
  • D. Daisy Chaining

Source

Study-guide sections

NET08 · Topology and failure reasoning

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET08 · Topology and failure reasoning

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

Correct answer: C — Ring in the conventional Token Ring association

NET08 associates token passing with Token Ring, so ring is the intended topology among these choices. The answer is an association rather than a universal claim: token passing is an access method and not every ring must use it. None of the other topology names inherently establishes token access.

Evidence in the complete study note

Bus uses a shared backbone; an unterminated break can disrupt the segment. Star connects endpoints through a central device: one edge failure isolates that endpoint, whereas central failure affects the star. Ring forms a loop; basic single rings are vulnerable to a break, while protected dual rings differ. Token passing is associated with Token Ring but is an access method, not a necessary property of every ring. Tree is hierarchical; hybrid combines arrangements.NET08
Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.NET14

Choice by choice

B · incorrect — A bus describes a shared backbone; token access is not inherent in that layout.

C · correct — Token Ring is the conventional association, with the caveat that tokens are an access method.

D · incorrect — Daisy chaining describes successive connections and does not by itself establish token passing.

Question 107

A __________ is a device that forwards packets between networks by processing the routing information included in the packet.

  • A. bridge
  • B. firewall
  • C. router
  • D. hub

Source

  • Data Communication & Networking practice questions · Question 11

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions.

Study-guide sections

NET11 · Routers, gateways and traffic controls

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET11 · Routers, gateways and traffic controls

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

Correct answer: C — router

Router forwarding explicitly compares the destination IP to routing table entries to choose the next path between networks. Evidence: PDF 12, 12, 12, 48.

Evidence in the complete study note

Routers forward IP packets between networks using destination prefixes and next hops. They separate broadcast domains and normally do not forward local link broadcasts. A default gateway is usually a router, while a protocol gateway can translate application formats; therefore a gateway is not inherently a device that implements every OSI layer.NET11
A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.NET09
A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.NET10

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Bridge filters same-protocol LAN traffic using MAC (PDF 12, 12, 12, 48.)

B · incorrect — A firewall permits/denies access; that is not the defining routing-table function (PDF 12, 12, 12, 48.)

C · correct — Router matches the stated destination-IP routing procedure (PDF 12, 12, 12, 48.)

D · incorrect — Hub repeats/broadcasts without destination-route analysis (PDF 12, 12, 12, 48.)

SCTP is a reliable message-oriented transport with multiple streams.NET17

Study-guide references

NET07 · Cables, wireless and connectors

Correct answer: C — optical fiber

Optical fiber guides light, resists electromagnetic interference and supports high-capacity, long-reach links with suitable optics and installation. Twisted pair and coaxial cable carry electrical signals; their shielding or pair geometry can reduce interference but does not give the medium optical immunity. Exact speeds depend on the selected specification and equipment, so this comparison does not rank every possible fiber and copper product by speed.

Evidence in the complete study note

Twisted pairs reduce coupled interference; UTP has no added shield and STP adds shielding. Coax has an inner conductor and outer shield sharing an axis. Fiber guides light and resists electromagnetic interference; it supports high capacity and long reach, but requires suitable optics and installation. Exact speed, cost and reach depend on the specification, not the material alone. Fiber can still be tapped.NET07

  • D. phase modulation

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

Correct answer: A — digital modulation

Digital modulation explicitly converts digital data to analog signals; ASK/FSK/PSK are its given methods. The other names are listed as analog modulation of analog data. Evidence: PDF 13.

Evidence in the complete study note

ASK varies carrier amplitude, FSK frequency, PSK phase; QAM combines amplitude and phase. AM/FM/PM can carry analog data. PCM digitizes analog input by sampling, quantizing and encoding. Sampling must exceed twice the highest retained baseband frequency in practical designs; b-bit samples have 2^b quantization levels and uncompressed rate fs×b. PAM/PWM are pulse modulation methods; pulse amplitude or width alone is not a binary PCM code.NET15
Analog signals vary continuously; digital signals use discrete symbol states. Data and signal types are separate: digital bits can modulate an analog carrier. A sine wave has amplitude, frequency and phase. Frequency f counts cycles/second, period T=1/f, and wavelength λ=v/f depends on propagation speed v. Phase specifies displacement within a cycle. Composite signals combine frequencies.NET04

Question 113

Which single option gives the complete set of listed operations that can be implemented as physical-layer transmission coding or modulation?

  • A. line coding
  • B. channel coding
  • C. modulation
  • D. all of the mentioned

NET15 · Line coding, modulation and sampling

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

NET15 · Line coding, modulation and sampling

Correct answer: D — all of the mentioned

Physical transmission includes mapping bits to signal patterns and modulating carriers. Channel coding in this question means redundancy used in transmission coding, rather than every possible higher-layer error-control mechanism. Under that scope, all three operations can be physical-layer work. Each individual choice names only part of the qualifying set, so the inclusive option is the complete response.

Evidence in the complete study note

A NIC supplies a computer’s network interface and commonly implements both physical and link functions. Calling a NIC a physical interface does not mean all its functions are layer 1. Physical specifications include connectors, signaling, voltage, timing and physical coding/modulation; the PHY interface to MAC handles hardware signaling.NET09
Line coding maps digital bits to digital signal patterns. NRZ uses levels without a forced mid-bit return; Manchester supplies a mid-bit transition for clocking, with bit convention specified. Differential Manchester encodes using transitions relative to previous state. AMI alternates the polarity of successive ones; pseudoternary alternates zero pulses. Block coding adds code redundancy; scrambling replaces problematic patterns without necessarily increasing bit count. Multilevel schemes include 2B1Q and 8B6T; MLT-3 uses a sequence of voltage transitions.NET15
ASK varies carrier amplitude, FSK frequency, PSK phase; QAM combines amplitude and phase. AM/FM/PM can carry analog data. PCM digitizes analog input by sampling, quantizing and encoding. Sampling must exceed twice the highest retained baseband frequency in practical designs; b-bit samples have 2^b quantization levels and uncompressed rate fs×b. PAM/PWM are pulse modulation methods; pulse amplitude or width alone is not a binary PCM code.NET15

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Line coding is physical signaling work, but alone omits the other qualifying operations.

B · incorrect — Physical channel coding adds transmission redundancy, but alone is incomplete.

C · incorrect — Modulation is a physical transmission operation, but alone is incomplete.

D · correct — Line coding, physical channel coding and modulation all qualify, making this the complete set.

Under the OSI role convention used here, which task belongs to physical transmission coding rather than data-link framing and control? Here channel coding means physical-channel coding, not a link-frame CRC or retransmission procedure.

  • A. framing
  • B. error control
  • C. flow control

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET13 · Link control, framing and error detection

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

Correct answer: D — channel coding

The data-link layer packages data into frames and can provide hop-local error and flow control. Physical transmission coding concerns how the channel carries the signal and any coding assigned to that physical role. The explicit convention distinguishes physical-channel coding from link error-detection redundancy or ARQ; without that scope, the broad term coding could overlap link functions.

Evidence in the complete study note

Link-layer LLC identifies or multiplexes upper-layer protocols and may supply link control; MAC handles medium-dependent addressing/access and frame delivery. Network addressing belongs to layer 3. Ethernet, PPP and HDLC are link protocols. Frame headers may carry addresses and control/type fields; synchronization and exact framing depend on the protocol.NET13
Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.NET14
A NIC supplies a computer’s network interface and commonly implements both physical and link functions. Calling a NIC a physical interface does not mean all its functions are layer 1. Physical specifications include connectors, signaling, voltage, timing and physical coding/modulation; the PHY interface to MAC handles hardware signaling.NET09

B · incorrect — Link error control includes detection and protocol-dependent recovery.

C · incorrect — Link flow control regulates hop-local sending when supported.

D · correct — Physical-channel coding is outside the stated link framing/control role.

CRC expands to Cyclic Redundancy Check.NET-S04
Detection adds redundancy but does not guarantee correction. Even parity adds a bit so the total number of ones is even: 1011 needs parity 1. It detects every odd number of bit flips but misses even counts. CRC treats bits as a polynomial and appends the XOR-division remainder; the receiver repeats the division. Internet checksums add words with end-around carry and complement the sum. A burst spans from the first corrupted bit through the last, including unchanged interior bits. Retransmission or sufficient forward-error-correcting redundancy is needed for recovery.NET13

Choice by choice

A · correct — Cyclic Redundancy Check is the exact listed phrase (PDF 13.)

B · incorrect — Code repeat check is not the expansion listed (PDF 13.)

C · incorrect — Code redundancy check changes Cyclic to Code (PDF 13.)

D · incorrect — Cyclic repeat check changes Redundancy to repeat (PDF 13.)
