Question 123

Which option gives the complete set of listed CSMA multiple-access mechanisms for shared-channel contention?

  • A. CSMA/CD
  • B. CSMA/CA
  • C. Both CSMA/CD & CSMA/CA
  • D. HDLC

Adapted from

  • Data Communication & Networking practice questions · Question 27

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify the requested service or delivery guarantee, then distinguish application roles, transport behavior and address configuration.

Study-guide sections

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

NET13 · Link control, framing and error detection

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

NET13 · Link control, framing and error detection

Correct answer: C — Both CSMA/CD & CSMA/CA

CSMA/CD and CSMA/CA both govern shared-medium access. Legacy half-duplex Ethernet uses collision detection and backoff, while Wi-Fi uses collision avoidance procedures with waiting, backoff and acknowledgments. Selecting only one omits another valid listed mechanism. HDLC is a link framing/control protocol rather than either of these CSMA contention mechanisms, so the combined CSMA option is complete.

Evidence in the complete study note

Random access allows contention: ALOHA sends opportunistically; CSMA senses before sending. In legacy half-duplex Ethernet, CSMA/CD detects collision, sends a jam indication, stops, and retries after random backoff. The jam signals a collision, not its clearance. Wi-Fi 802.11 uses CSMA/CA with waiting/backoff and acknowledgments; sensing does not eliminate hidden-terminal collisions.NET14
Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.NET14
Link-layer LLC identifies or multiplexes upper-layer protocols and may supply link control; MAC handles medium-dependent addressing/access and frame delivery. Network addressing belongs to layer 3. Ethernet, PPP and HDLC are link protocols. Frame headers may carry addresses and control/type fields; synchronization and exact framing depend on the protocol.NET13

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — CSMA/CD is a valid mechanism but omits the other listed CSMA mechanism.

B · incorrect — CSMA/CA is a valid mechanism but omits the other listed CSMA mechanism.

C · correct — This includes both listed CSMA contention mechanisms.

D · incorrect — HDLC is a link framing/control protocol, not a listed CSMA medium-contention mechanism.

Question 125

For IPv4 as described in the note, which listed function is not provided by IP itself? Here “error control” means header checksum error detection.

  • A. routing
  • B. inter-networking
  • C. congestion control
  • D. error control

Adapted from

  • Data Communication & Networking practice questions · Question 29

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate address width, syntax, reserved scope and the supplied prefix or historical classful convention.

Study-guide sections

NET16 · Network delivery and IPv4 header

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

NET30 · Routing algorithms and destination sets

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET16 · Network delivery and IPv4 header

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

NET30 · Routing algorithms and destination sets

Correct answer: C — congestion control

IPv4 supports logical packet delivery across networks, including routing, and checks its header with a checksum. The use of error control therefore refers to detection, not reliable end-to-end recovery. TCP supplies congestion control to protect network capacity; IPv4 itself does not provide TCP’s congestion-control service. The question separates those protocol services instead of denying that the network layer ever detects errors.

Evidence in the complete study note

The IPv4 checksum protects its header; IP does not lack error checking altogether. Identification, flags and offset support fragmentation. IPv4 sources and routers may fragment when allowed; reassembly occurs at the destination. If DF is set and the next MTU is too small, forwarding fails and an ICMP diagnostic may be returned.NET16
TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.NET17
Routing computes paths; forwarding chooses a next hop for an individual packet. Select the matching route with the longest prefix, then apply the routing system’s tie-breaking criteria. A default /0 matches when nothing more specific does. Static routes are configured; dynamic protocols exchange reachability. Distance vector uses neighbor estimates, while link state distributes link information and computes shortest paths. Interior protocols operate within an autonomous system; BGP exchanges routes between systems.NET30

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Routing is explicitly a network-layer function, so it cannot be the requested exception.

B · incorrect — Forwarding packets between networks is an established network-layer responsibility.

C · correct — Congestion control of the kind protecting network capacity is a TCP service rather than a service supplied by IPv4 itself.

D · incorrect — IPv4 detects header corruption with its checksum, so error detection is present under the stated meaning.

Question 128

In a multi-destination scheme that carries an explicit list of multiple selected targets in each packet, which statements are incorrect as general descriptions? Select all that apply.

  • B. contains the list of all destinations
  • C. data is not sent by packets
  • D. there are multiple receivers

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET30 · Routing algorithms and destination sets

Correct answers (select all): A, C — is same as broadcast routing; data is not sent by packets

A packet can carry a list identifying several selected destinations without addressing every destination in the broadcast scope. That makes universal equivalence with broadcasting false. The scheme is explicitly packet-based, so saying data are not sent by packets is also false. The list of targets and the presence of multiple receivers are true descriptions and therefore are not selected in this negative question.

Evidence in the complete study note

Flooding sends copies on eligible outgoing links with duplicate/lifetime controls; random walk picks a neighbor probabilistically. Unicast targets one destination, broadcast all in a scope, multicast a subscribed group and anycast one member sharing an address, normally nearest under routing metrics. Group multicast trees use mechanisms such as reverse-path checks; Ethernet spanning tree is a different layer-2 mechanism.NET30

D · incorrect — Multiple targeted receivers are the defining destination-set property, so this statement is not incorrect.

Question 134

For one TCP connection, which single option gives the complete set of correct descriptions?

  • A. is a connection-oriented protocol
  • B. uses a three way handshake to establish a connection
  • C. receives data from application as a single stream
  • D. all of the mentioned

  • Data Communication & Networking practice questions · Question 38

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET18 · Trace the TCP handshake

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Correct answer: D — all of the mentioned

TCP establishes logical transport connection state through the SYN, SYN+ACK and ACK exchange. It then provides an ordered byte-stream service for that connection rather than preserving individual application message boundaries. All three descriptions apply to one TCP connection. Each individual response is therefore incomplete under the complete-set instruction, while the inclusive option collects all of the valid properties.

Evidence in the complete study note

TCP establishes state with SYN, SYN+ACK, then ACK. SYN consumes one sequence position even with no application bytes. An acknowledgment states the next expected sequence number. For client ISN=395 and server ISN=260: client sends SYN seq395; server sends SYN+ACK seq260 ack396; client sends ACK seq396 ack261. Later byte counts advance sequence numbers. FIN also consumes one sequence position.NET18
TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.NET17

B · incorrect — TCP uses a three-way handshake, but that alone is an incomplete set.

C · incorrect — TCP accepts an application byte stream within a connection, but this alone is incomplete.

D · correct — Connection orientation, three-way setup and a per-connection byte stream are all valid.

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

Correct answer: B — Circuit switched

Assuming the traditional local circuit telephone network, call setup creates a dedicated circuit and teardown releases it. This identifies circuit switching.

Evidence in the complete study note

Circuit switching sets up a path with reserved resources, transfers data, then releases it. Predictable allocated bandwidth trades against setup/blocking and wasted reservation during silence. A traditional telephone call is the standard example. Packet switching divides data into packets that share links statistically; queueing can add variable delay and loss. This does not make modern voice-over-packet impossible: buffering, scheduling and capacity planning manage it.NET31

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Packet switching is discrete packet communication

B · correct — Circuit switching matches the traditional dedicated-call assumption

C · incorrect — Bit switched is not a listed switching category

D · incorrect — Line switched is not a listed switching category

Question 138

Most packet switches use this principle ____________

  • A. Stop and wait
  • B. Store and forward
  • C. Store and wait
  • D. Stop and forward

Source

  • Data Communication & Networking practice questions · Question 42

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions.

Study-guide sections

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

Correct answer: B — Store and forward

Packet store-and-forward means receiving the complete packet or frame before forwarding it. That is the switching principle named by B. Stop-and-wait is instead a reliability procedure that sends one frame and waits for acknowledgment. Cut-through alternatives exist, so the answer identifies the conventional principle without claiming every switch must use it.

Evidence in the complete study note

Datagram packets are forwarded independently. Virtual circuits establish forwarding state, but resource reservation is optional, not a necessary property of every virtual circuit. Message switching stores a complete message before forwarding, without a dedicated end-to-end path. Packet store-and-forward waits for the full packet/frame; cut-through starts after enough header arrives; fragment-free historically waits through the initial collision-sensitive portion. No routing algorithm guarantees that every packet always takes the geometrically shortest route.NET31
Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.NET14

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Stop-and-wait is a link reliability/flow procedure involving acknowledgments, not the switching-buffering principle.

B · correct — Store-and-forward buffers the full packet or frame before sending it on the next link.

C · incorrect — Store and wait is not the defined switching principle named in NET31.

D · incorrect — Stop and forward is not the defined receive-complete-then-forward switching procedure.

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET21 · Web, file, mail and remote-login protocols

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Correct answer: D — TCP

TCP is explicitly transport, whereas SMTP/FTP and the HTTP service belong to the application side. Evidence: PDF 18, 18, 28.

Evidence in the complete study note

HTTP defines web request/response semantics; it is stateless, and a message body may be absent. HTTPS adds TLS protection. FTP transfers files using control and separate data connections; it is not the same protocol as SFTP. SMTP submits and relays mail; POP3 retrieves messages and IMAP accesses/synchronizes server mailboxes. Saying SMTP handles both sending and end-user mailbox retrieval is inaccurate.NET21
TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.NET17

Choice by choice

B · incorrect — SMTP is in the application protocol list (PDF 18, 18, 28.)

C · incorrect — FTP is explicitly application file transfer (PDF 18, 18, 28.)

D · correct — TCP is explicitly a transport protocol (PDF 18, 18, 28.)

Question 145

In TCP connection establishment procedure, if a client chooses Initial Sequence Number of 395, and server chooses 260, then:

  • A. The 1st segment sent will contain sequence number of 396
  • B. The 2nd segment sent will contain acknowledgement number of 261
  • C. The 3rd segment sent will contain sequence number of 261
  • D. The 2nd segment sent will contain acknowledgement number of 396
  • E. The 2nd segment sent will contain sequence number of 395
  • F. The 3rd segment sent will contain acknowledgement number of 396

Source

  • Mock exam 3 · Question 4

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Trace the handshake in order, keeping each endpoint’s sequence and acknowledgment fields separate.

Study-guide sections

NET18 · Trace the TCP handshake

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET18 · Trace the TCP handshake

Correct answer: D — Second segment acknowledgment number 396

SYN consumes one sequence position. The first segment is client SYN seq395. The server’s second segment is SYN+ACK seq260 ack396, acknowledging the client SYN. The third is client ACK seq396 ack261. Comparing those fields shows only D matches; sequence numbers and acknowledgment numbers must not be swapped between endpoints.

Evidence in the complete study note

TCP establishes state with SYN, SYN+ACK, then ACK. SYN consumes one sequence position even with no application bytes. An acknowledgment states the next expected sequence number. For client ISN=395 and server ISN=260: client sends SYN seq395; server sends SYN+ACK seq260 ack396; client sends ACK seq396 ack261. Later byte counts advance sequence numbers. FIN also consumes one sequence position.NET18

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — The first client SYN uses its initial sequence number 395, not the next position 396.

B · incorrect — The second segment acknowledges the client SYN with 396; 261 is the later acknowledgment of the server SYN.

C · incorrect — The third segment’s sequence number is the client’s next position 396, not the server acknowledgment value 261.

D · correct — The server’s SYN+ACK acknowledges client ISN 395 plus one, giving 396.

E · incorrect — The second segment is sent by the server with its own sequence number 260.

F · incorrect — The third segment acknowledges server ISN 260 plus one, giving 261 rather than 396.

For IPv4 when fragmentation is permitted, which option gives the complete set of nodes that may fragment packets and the location of reassembly?

  • A. Fragment at the source host; re-assemble at the destination host
  • B. Fragment at the source host and routers; re-assemble at the destination host
  • C. Fragment at the source host and routers; re-assemble at the routers and destination host
  • D. Fragment at the source host; re-assemble at the routers and destination host
  • E. IP does not support Fragmentation and Re-assembly.

Study-guide sections

NET16 · Network delivery and IPv4 header

NET23 · Special ranges, private addresses and IPv6

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET16 · Network delivery and IPv4 header

NET23 · Special ranges, private addresses and IPv6

Correct answer: B — Fragment at the source host and routers; re-assemble at the destination host

IPv4 permits both the source and a router to fragment packets when fragmentation is allowed and an outgoing MTU requires it. The destination reassembles the fragments. Source-only fragmentation omits a permitted IPv4 case; it instead resembles the IPv6 restriction. Adding intermediate-router reassembly is incorrect. Naming IPv4 and asking for the complete permitted set makes the version-specific distinction explicit.

Evidence in the complete study note

The IPv4 checksum protects its header; IP does not lack error checking altogether. Identification, flags and offset support fragmentation. IPv4 sources and routers may fragment when allowed; reassembly occurs at the destination. If DF is set and the next MTU is too small, forwarding fails and an ICMP diagnostic may be returned.NET16
IPv6 has 128-bit hexadecimal addresses, flexible prefixes and no IPv4-style broadcast. Sources, not routers, fragment IPv6 packets. IPv6 does not automatically encrypt traffic or make authentication unnecessary. Compare IPv6’s larger 128-bit address space and encryption support separately; specify the property being evaluated.NET23

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — A source may fragment, but this option omits permitted IPv4 router fragmentation.

B · correct — IPv4 sources and routers may fragment; only the destination reassembles.

C · incorrect — Neither cited IP fragmentation rule places reassembly at intermediate routers.

D · incorrect — Destination reassembly is required; the additional router reassembly claim is unsupported for either version.

E · incorrect — Both version-specific rules support fragmentation and reassembly, although the allowed fragmenting nodes differ.

Study-guide references

NET08 · Topology and failure reasoning

Correct answer: F — Failure of a special node results in no stations being able to communicate

The star description explicitly calls its hub/switch a single point of failure: failure of that central device brings the whole system down. Ordinary station/link failure is isolated. Evidence: PDF 23, 23, 23, 23.

Evidence in the complete study note

Star connects endpoints through a central device: one edge failure isolates that endpoint, whereas central failure affects the star. Token passing is associated with Token Ring but is an access method, not a necessary property of every ring. Tree is hierarchical; hybrid combines arrangements.NET08

Question 149

For IPv4 networks, distinguish interface IP addresses, transport port numbers and the IPv4 Protocol header field. Which statement is true?

  • A. The protocol number commonly used by web server applications is 80
  • B. Every application must use a well-known port number
  • C. Each host and router in the Internet has only a single IP address
  • D. Client applications may dynamically select port numbers
  • E. A protocol number is used to indicate the version of IP being used

Adapted from

  • Mock exam 2 · Question 20

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify the requested service or delivery guarantee, then distinguish application roles, transport behavior and address configuration.

Study-guide sections

NET-S06 · Interface addresses and transport-number namespaces

NET16 · Network delivery and IPv4 header

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET-S06 · Interface addresses and transport-number namespaces

NET16 · Network delivery and IPv4 header

Correct answer: D — Client applications may dynamically select port numbers

Client applications commonly use dynamically selected ephemeral ports. Ports identify transport endpoints, whereas the IPv4 Protocol field identifies the carried upper-layer protocol, such as TCP or UDP. The separate Version field identifies the IP version. Port 80 is a usual HTTP service port, not an IP protocol number. Hosts and routers can have multiple addressed interfaces, so they are not restricted to one IP address.

Evidence in the complete study note

An IP address identifies a network interface rather than limiting a whole computer to one address. A computer or router can have several interfaces and addresses. Under a supplied IPv4 prefix, leading bits identify the network and the remaining bits identify an address within that network; a MAC address is a separate link-layer identifier.NET-S06
TCP and UDP port fields are 16 bits, allowing numbers from 0 through 65535. Well-known ports are 0–1023, registered ports are 1024–49151, and dynamic/private ports are 49152–65535. Client endpoints can use dynamically selected ports instead of every application requiring a well-known assignment. These port numbers are distinct from the IP version and upper-protocol fields.NET-S06
IP supplies connectionless best-effort packet delivery, not end-to-end ordering or retransmission. IPv4 addresses are 32 bits. Its minimum header is 20 bytes and can grow to 60 bytes; it is not a 32-bit header. IHL counts 32-bit words; total length includes header and payload. TTL limits lifetime across routers; the protocol field identifies TCP, UDP or another upper-layer protocol.NET16

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — 80 is a usual HTTP port number, not the IPv4 Protocol value for HTTP.

B · incorrect — Clients may use ephemeral ports, so a well-known port is not mandatory for every application.

C · incorrect — A device can have multiple addressed interfaces and therefore multiple IP addresses.

D · correct — Clients may dynamically select ephemeral transport ports.

E · incorrect — The IPv4 Protocol field identifies the upper-layer protocol; the Version field identifies the IP version.

Study-guide sections

NET02 · Network size, access and architecture

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET02 · Network size, access and architecture

Correct answer: B — Intranet

The relevant distinction is who can access organizational services, rather than how far the links extend. An intranet serves an organization internally, so it can include both local and wide-area components. LAN, WAN and MAN describe geographic reach and cannot replace that access-scope classification. The option identifies an intranet without assuming a particular geographic footprint.

Evidence in the complete study note

PAN connects personal devices, such as Bluetooth accessories. LAN covers a local building or campus; MAN spans a metropolitan region; WAN connects distant regions. Device count alone does not determine the category. The Internet is a global network of networks, commonly the largest example of a WAN.NET02
An intranet serves an organization internally; an extranet exposes selected services to approved outsiders. Neither term alone specifies geographic size. A client requests a service; a server supplies it. Peer systems may perform both roles. Dedicated servers concentrate on service workloads but can still be clients of DNS, backup or update services. A ten-user cutoff is a teaching guideline, not a technical law. Centralization simplifies administration but creates dependencies; peer networks still need security.NET02

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — LAN describes geographic reach of local components rather than the organizational access scope requested.

B · correct — An intranet serves the university’s internal members across its constituent networks.

C · incorrect — WAN describes geographic reach of some components rather than the internal-access scope requested.

D · incorrect — MAN describes metropolitan geographic reach rather than internal organizational access.

Study-guide sections

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

Correct answer: D — Data-link forwarding functions, with NICs also implementing PHY

Bridges and ordinary switches inspect MAC frames at layer 2. A NIC commonly implements both physical and data-link functions, as NET09 explains; listing NICs here does not force all NIC work into one layer. D is the common frame/addressing layer for the listed devices’ relevant network-interface forwarding functions.

Evidence in the complete study note

A NIC supplies a computer’s network interface and commonly implements both physical and link functions. Calling a NIC a physical interface does not mean all its functions are layer 1. Physical specifications include connectors, signaling, voltage, timing and physical coding/modulation; the PHY interface to MAC handles hardware signaling.NET09
A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.NET10

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — A NIC has physical functions, but bridges/switches make layer-2 forwarding decisions beyond signal repetition.

B · incorrect — These devices’ MAC/frame operations are below application-service semantics.

C · incorrect — Ordinary bridges and Ethernet switches do not route IP prefixes as their defining function.

D · correct — Bridges/switches operate at layer 2, and NICs also implement link-layer MAC/frame functions.

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

NET-S04 · Computer networks and network interfaces

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

NET-S04 · Computer networks and network interfaces

Correct answer: B — Network printer

A network printer is an endpoint resource that receives client jobs. A router forwards packets between networks, a wireless access point normally bridges wireless and wired link traffic, and a hub repeats physical signals among ports. These are intermediary roles in the comparison. The question classifies their normal function rather than claiming that an intermediary cannot also expose a management endpoint.

Evidence in the complete study note

A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.NET09
A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.NET10
A computer network connects computers or other devices so they can exchange information and share resources such as files, storage and printers. The interconnection uses both hardware and software; neither hardware alone nor software alone is the definition of the whole network.NET-S04

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Routers forward traffic between networks and are intermediaries.

B · correct — A network printer is the client-facing end resource.

C · incorrect — A wireless access point normally bridges wireless and wired link traffic.

D · incorrect — A hub repeats signals between attached devices and is an intermediary.

Correct answer: D — Scalability

Scalability is explicitly continued predictable function as system size grows, matching expansion without undermining existing service. Evidence: PDF 32.

Evidence in the complete study note

Delivery means reaching the intended recipient; accuracy means preserving content; timeliness means meeting a deadline; jitter means variation in arrival delay. Throughput measures achieved transfer rate, reliability measures dependable operation, and security concerns unauthorized actions. Scalability means accommodating growth without unacceptable service degradation.NET01
Quality of service (QoS) controls traffic treatment to meet objectives such as throughput, delay, jitter or loss. Classification, queue scheduling and allocation of buffer or bandwidth resources implement such treatment. QoS concerns delivered service behavior; scalability concerns accommodating growth, and security concerns unauthorized actions.NET-S02

Question 157

Which statement is incorrect when packet switching means connectionless datagram switching?

  • A. In packet switching, messages are sent in small blocks
  • B. In packet switching, an end-to-end connection has to be established
  • C. In circuit switching, a channel is dedicatedly used
  • D. For bursty traffic, statistical packet sharing can use capacity that dedicated circuits would reserve while idle.

Adapted from

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · Question 16-4

  • National Computer Science Exit Exam · Question 97

  • National Computer Science Exit Exam

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam

  • Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 149

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions.

Study-guide sections

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

Correct answer: B — In packet switching, an end-to-end connection has to be established

Datagram switching divides messages into packets and forwards those packets independently without requiring end-to-end connection establishment. Circuit switching reserves resources along a path. Statistical sharing lets bursty packet traffic use capacity that would otherwise remain reserved but idle; this is a conditional utilization advantage, not a universal claim that packets outperform circuits for every workload or metric.

Evidence in the complete study note

Circuit switching sets up a path with reserved resources, transfers data, then releases it. Predictable allocated bandwidth trades against setup/blocking and wasted reservation during silence. A traditional telephone call is the standard example. Packet switching divides data into packets that share links statistically; queueing can add variable delay and loss. This does not make modern voice-over-packet impossible: buffering, scheduling and capacity planning manage it.NET31
Datagram packets are forwarded independently. Virtual circuits establish forwarding state, but resource reservation is optional, not a necessary property of every virtual circuit. Message switching stores a complete message before forwarding, without a dedicated end-to-end path. Packet store-and-forward waits for the full packet/frame; cut-through starts after enough header arrives; fragment-free historically waits through the initial collision-sensitive portion. No routing algorithm guarantees that every packet always takes the geometrically shortest route.NET31

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Packet switching divides messages into smaller packets.

B · correct — Connectionless datagrams do not require end-to-end connection setup.

C · incorrect — Circuit switching reserves channel resources for the connection.

D · incorrect — For bursty traffic, shared packet links can avoid idle dedicated reservations; the qualified statement is true.

Correct answer: A — Transport layer

Evidence in the complete study note

Ports identify transport endpoints; the application can choose a transport and request socket buffer sizes, subject to OS limits. A TCP connection is identified by source/destination IP and source/destination port, with TCP understood. IPv4 protocol numbers identify upper protocols; 80 is a usual HTTP port, not an IP protocol number. Clients often use ephemeral ports. A router removes a received link frame, inspects IP, and creates a new link frame for the next hop. MAC addresses usually change across routed hops; end-to-end IP addresses ordinarily remain until translation.NET12

Bus explicitly connects all devices to a central backbone cable terminated at both ends. Evidence: PDF 23, 23, 23, 23.

Evidence in the complete study note

Bus uses a shared backbone; an unterminated break can disrupt the segment. Star connects endpoints through a central device: one edge failure isolates that endpoint, whereas central failure affects the star. Question 163

In data communication, data rate refers how fast we can send data and is measured in bits per second. Which one of the following is not a factor for data rate?

  • A. Travel distance
  • B. Levels of the signals [SS
  • C. Bandwidth available
  • D. Level of noise

Source

  • Computer Science Exit Exam · Sene 2016 · Question 30-1

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule.

Study-guide sections

NET05 · Bit rate, baud and channel capacity

NET06 · Delay, impairments and transmission modes

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET05 · Bit rate, baud and channel capacity

NET06 · Delay, impairments and transmission modes

Correct answer: A — Travel distance is not an explicit channel-capacity formula variable

NET05 gives Nyquist in terms of bandwidth and signal states, and Shannon in terms of bandwidth and signal-to-noise ratio. Distance is not an independent variable in those simplified capacity formulas, so A is the intended comparison. It can still affect practical achievable rate through attenuation and delay. The image confirms travel distance despite noise in another extracted option.

Evidence in the complete study note

For an ideal noiseless channel, Nyquist gives R≤2B log2(M). For Gaussian noise, Shannon gives C=B log2(1+S/N), with a linear power ratio; SNR(dB)=10 log10(S/N). Bandwidth, signal levels and noise appear explicitly. Distance affects attenuation, delay and often achievable rate, but is not a separate variable in these simplified capacity formulas.NET05
Transmission delay is packet bits divided by link bit rate; propagation delay is distance divided by signal speed. Processing and queueing add delay. A 1000-byte packet takes 0.8 ms to serialize at 10 Mbit/s; increasing line rate does not reduce propagation time.NET06

Choice by choice

A · correct — Distance is absent as an independent variable in the simplified formulas, although it affects real links indirectly.

B · incorrect — The number of signal levels appears explicitly in Nyquist through log2(M).

C · incorrect — Available bandwidth directly appears as B in both Nyquist and Shannon capacity expressions.

D · incorrect — Noise affects signal-to-noise ratio and therefore the Shannon capacity limit.

Question 164

Which layer of the OSI model ensures that the whole message (group of packets) arrives at the destination intact and in order?

  • A. Session layer
  • B. Transport layer
  • C. Data link layer
  • D. Network layer

Sources

  • Computer Science Exit Exam · Sene 2016 · Question 30-2

  • Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 165

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.

Study-guide sections

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

Correct answer: B — Transport layer

Transport explicitly makes process-delivered data intact and ordered, using sequence-numbered segments and end-to-end error control. Evidence: PDF 16, 15, 15, 16.

Evidence in the complete study note

TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.NET17
Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.NET14
OSI session roles establish/manage dialogs and can coordinate checkpoints so transfer resumes after interruption. Presentation roles translate encodings and handle compression/encryption. Compression reduces representation size; encryption hides content and need not shrink it. Application protocols provide services directly to applications. Practical implementations distribute these functions differently; TLS is not proof of a separate physical presentation-layer device.NET19

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Session controls dialogs/checkpoints (PDF 16, 15, 15, 16.)

B · correct — Transport explicitly ensures intact and ordered whole-message delivery (PDF 16, 15, 15, 16.)

C · incorrect — Data link controls hop-to-hop frames rather than the entire end-to-end message (PDF 16, 15, 15, 16.)

D · incorrect — Network packets can arrive out of order (PDF 16, 15, 15, 16.)

Question 165

Which of the following is not a valid host address within the network 172.17.128.0/21 ?

  • A. 172.17.128.1/21
  • B. 172.17.135.255 /21
  • C. 172.17.135.0 /21
  • D. 172.17.128.255/21

Source

  • Computer Science model exam collection · Question 5

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule.

Study-guide sections

NET25 · Find subnet bounds and usable hosts

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET25 · Find subnet bounds and usable hosts

Correct answer: B — 172.17.135.255/21 is broadcast

A /21 groups eight third-octet values, here 128–135. The network is 172.17.128.0 and its broadcast is 172.17.135.255. B sets every host bit to one and cannot be assigned to an ordinary host. The other choices are inside the usable range; ending in .0 or .255 alone does not make an address reserved.

Evidence in the complete study note

For ordinary broadcast LANs let h=32-p. Total addresses=2^h; usable hosts=2^h-2, reserving network and directed broadcast. Find the changing octet’s increment as 256-mask octet, round the address down to a multiple, and extend through the next boundary minus one.NET25
192.168.2.64/26 spans .64–.127; usable .65–.126 gives 62 hosts. 192.168.10.25/28 spans .16–.31, so its network is .16. 172.17.128.0/21 spans 172.17.128.0–172.17.135.255; .128.255 and .135.0 are valid interior hosts, but .135.255 is broadcast. /27 gives 32 total and 30 usable, not 32 usable.NET25

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — 172.17.128.1 is one above the network boundary and is a valid usable host.

B · correct — 172.17.135.255 sets all eleven host bits to one and is the subnet broadcast address.

C · incorrect — 172.17.135.0 is inside the /21 block; its host bits are not all zero or all one.

D · incorrect — 172.17.128.255 is an interior host; the .255 ending alone does not make it /21 broadcast.

NET07 · Cables, wireless and connectors

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET07 · Cables, wireless and connectors

NET-S07 · Physical signaling and legacy Ethernet cable roles

Correct answer: C — Switch-to-PC normally uses straight-through cable in legacy Ethernet

Under the legacy MDI/MDI-X convention, a switch port and PC have unlike roles and use straight-through cable. PCs and router Ethernet endpoints conventionally share the endpoint role, while two switches share the switch role, so those like-role links use crossover. Auto-MDI-X can remove the practical requirement; the question is testing the conventional cable-role distinction.

Evidence in the complete study note

Radio, microwave and infrared are unguided media. Ground waves follow Earth, sky waves can reflect from ionized layers, and line-of-sight paths require suitable visibility. Microwaves are radio waves in the broader physical classification. Infrared generally does not penetrate walls. Directionality depends on antennas: omnidirectional means broad azimuth coverage, not equal radiation in every 3-D direction. Legacy Ethernet straight-through cables join unlike MDI/MDI-X roles; crossover joins like roles, such as PC–PC or switch–switch. Auto-MDI-X can remove that requirement.NET07
For legacy fixed Ethernet port roles, PCs and router Ethernet endpoints use the same endpoint role, while ordinary switch ports use the opposite role. Thus a direct router-to-PC link uses crossover wiring; PC-to-switch or router-to-switch uses straight-through wiring. Automatic MDI-X can remove the need to choose the crossover manually.NET-S07

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — A legacy router Ethernet endpoint and PC have like interface roles, so crossover is appropriate.

B · incorrect — Two legacy switch ports have like roles and conventionally require crossover.

C · correct — Switch and PC have unlike legacy interface roles and normally use straight-through cable.

D · incorrect — Two PCs have like legacy interface roles; NET07 explicitly names PC–PC as a crossover example.

Study-guide sections

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

Correct answer: D — Stop and retry after random backoff

NET14 gives the collision sequence: detect, jam, stop and retry after random backoff. The jam indicates the collision itself, not that it has cleared. There is no router-coordinated clearance procedure or electrical clearance pulse in the stated rule. Therefore waiting for a delay and attempting transmission again is the supported host behavior.

Evidence in the complete study note

Random access allows contention: ALOHA sends opportunistically; CSMA senses before sending. In legacy half-duplex Ethernet, CSMA/CD detects collision, sends a jam indication, stops, and retries after random backoff. The jam signals a collision, not its clearance. Wi-Fi 802.11 uses CSMA/CA with waiting/backoff and acknowledgments; sensing does not eliminate hidden-terminal collisions.NET14
Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.NET14

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — The defined procedure uses collision indication and backoff; it does not include a collision-cleared electrical pulse.

B · incorrect — Ethernet collision recovery is performed by the hosts’ MAC procedure, not a router clearance signal.

C · incorrect — A jam announces the collision; it does not certify that the shared medium is clear.

D · correct — After stopping, hosts retry following random backoff, matching a delay before another transmission attempt.

Question 168

Which of the following is true regarding the use of switches and hubs for network connectivity in the network?

  • A. Switches increase the number of collision domains in the network
  • B. Switches take less time to process frames than hubs take
  • C. Switches do not forward broadcasts
  • D. Hubs can filter frames

Source

  • Computer Science model exam collection · Question 41

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions.

Study-guide sections

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

Correct answer: A — Switch ports separate collision domains

NET10 says each switch port separates collision domains, whereas a half-duplex hub repeats traffic into one shared collision domain. Switches still flood broadcasts within their VLAN, and hubs do not inspect and filter destination frames. The note gives no universal switch-versus-hub processing-time advantage, so A is the supported claim.

Evidence in the complete study note

Each switch port separates collision domains; full-duplex point-to-point Ethernet has no collisions and does not use CSMA/CD. Switching permits independent conversations simultaneously. Broadcasts still reach the VLAN unless another control filters them. A layer-3 switch also routes, so device marketing names do not override the function being examined.NET10
A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.NET09

Choice by choice

A · correct — Replacing a shared hub segment with separate switch ports divides the network into additional collision domains.

B · incorrect — The note establishes no universal lower switch processing time; a hub simply repeats signals.

C · incorrect — Switches flood broadcasts within the VLAN unless another control filters them.

D · incorrect — Hubs repeat physical signals and neither learn MAC destinations nor filter frames.

The TCP/IP Internet layer corresponds to OSI network and provides IP addressing/source-to-destination transmission with routing. Evidence: PDF 17, 15, 17.

Evidence in the complete study note

The four-layer TCP/IP model folds OSI layers 5–7 into application, retains transport, calls layer 3 Internet, and combines link/physical as network access. A model is a guide to functions, not a guarantee that every application gets a reliable network. Distinguish end-to-end application service from its underlying process-to-process transport.NET19

Question 171

Which of the following is not a primary function of the network layer in the OSI model?

  • A. Routing
  • B. Addressing
  • C. Flow control
  • D. Fragmentation

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 474

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.

Study-guide sections

NET16 · Network delivery and IPv4 header

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET16 · Network delivery and IPv4 header

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Correct answer: C — Flow control is not a primary network-layer duty

The network layer supplies logical addressing/routing and, for IPv4, fragmentation when permitted. Flow control instead protects a receiver in transport or hop-local link procedures, as NET14 and NET17 explain. Thus C is not a primary network-layer function in this layer model, without claiming that all control mechanisms belong exclusively to one layer.

Evidence in the complete study note

The IPv4 checksum protects its header; IP does not lack error checking altogether. Identification, flags and offset support fragmentation. IPv4 sources and routers may fragment when allowed; reassembly occurs at the destination. If DF is set and the next MTU is too small, forwarding fails and an ICMP diagnostic may be returned.NET16
Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.NET14
TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.NET17

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Routing is explicitly a main network-layer duty in the NET12 layer table.

B · incorrect — Logical addressing is explicitly assigned to the network layer.

C · correct — Receiver flow control is described at link and transport scope rather than as a primary network duty.

D · incorrect — NET16 supports IPv4 fragmentation by sources and routers, a network-protocol function.

Study-guide references

NET20 · DNS, DHCP and address resolution

NET12 · OSI layers and encapsulation

Correct answer: A — To identify a device within a local area network (LAN)

The module physical MAC address is imprinted on a NIC and used for local physical delivery; it is not encryption or the IP routing address. Evidence: PDF 17, 15.

Evidence in the complete study note

ARP resolves an on-link IPv4 next hop to a link address, using a broadcast request and normally unicast reply. For an off-subnet target, ARP resolves the gateway, not the remote target’s MAC. It bridges the network/link addressing boundary and is often classified at the link layer; calling ARP simply a network protocol uses a loose textbook convention. RARP reverses hardware-to-IP lookup; BOOTP/DHCP support boot configuration. ICMP reports errors and diagnostics; IGMP manages IPv4 multicast membership. These are separate companion protocols, not four pieces whose combination is IP.NET20
A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.NET10
Sending proceeds from application data to transport segment/datagram, network packet, link frame and physical bits/symbols; receiving reverses the order. Each layer serves the layer above. A router removes a received link frame, inspects IP, and creates a new link frame for the next hop. MAC addresses usually change across routed hops; end-to-end IP addresses ordinarily remain until translation.NET12

Study-guide sections

NET08 · Topology and failure reasoning

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET08 · Topology and failure reasoning

Correct answer: D — Mesh topology

Mesh has redundant interconnections and a single link failure does not affect the entire network. Bus backbone, ring break and star center failure are explicit vulnerabilities. Evidence: PDF 23, 24, 23, 23, 23.

Evidence in the complete study note

Bus uses a shared backbone; an unterminated break can disrupt the segment. Star connects endpoints through a central device: one edge failure isolates that endpoint, whereas central failure affects the star. Ring forms a loop; basic single rings are vulnerable to a break, while protected dual rings differ. Token passing is associated with Token Ring but is an access method, not a necessary property of every ring. Tree is hierarchical; hybrid combines arrangements.NET08
A full undirected mesh of n nodes needs n(n-1)/2 links and n-1 interfaces per node. For 50 nodes: 50×49/2=1225 links. Redundant paths improve fault tolerance at greater cable and interface cost.NET08

B · incorrect — A break/disabled station can disable a ring (PDF 23, 24, 23, 23, 23.)

D · correct — Redundant mesh paths support the strongest listed fault tolerance (PDF 23, 24, 23, 23, 23.)

Which listed terms describe IPv6’s flexible-prefix addressing or operations supported by that approach? Select all that apply.

  • A. Classful addressing
  • B. Classless addressing
  • C. Subnetting
  • D. CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing)

Study-guide sections

NET23 · Special ranges, private addresses and IPv6

NET26 · Borrow bits and choose a mask

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET23 · Special ranges, private addresses and IPv6

NET28 · Point-to-point links and route aggregation

NET26 · Borrow bits and choose a mask

Correct answers (select all): B, C, D — Classless addressing; Subnetting; CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing)

IPv6 uses flexible network prefixes rather than historical IPv4 address classes. Classless addressing describes this approach, subnetting divides prefixes into smaller networks, and CIDR terminology expresses classless prefixes and aggregation. These are compatible descriptions or operations rather than mutually exclusive schemes. The selection instruction therefore permits all three while excluding the classful A/B/C allocation model associated with historical IPv4.

Evidence in the complete study note

IPv6 has 128-bit hexadecimal addresses, flexible prefixes and no IPv4-style broadcast. Sources, not routers, fragment IPv6 packets. IPv6 does not automatically encrypt traffic or make authentication unnecessary. Compare IPv6’s larger 128-bit address space and encryption support separately; specify the property being evaluated.NET23
CIDR, Classless Inter-Domain Routing, replaces rigid class allocation and supports aggregation. Combine contiguous aligned blocks sharing leading bits; unrelated adjacent-looking labels may not aggregate cleanly. Four consecutive /26 blocks covering a /24 summarize to /24. More-specific routes must remain available where the aggregate would otherwise send traffic to the wrong next hop.NET28
To split parent /a into equal /p blocks, borrow b=p-a bits and obtain 2^b subnets. Do not subtract two subnets under modern practice. For a Class B /16 parent split to /19, b=3 gives eight subnets, each with 8192 addresses and 8190 conventional hosts. A /19 alone does not state its parent.NET26

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Historical classful A/B/C IPv4 defaults are not the IPv6 flexible-prefix scheme.

B · correct — IPv6 uses flexible prefixes rather than fixed historical address classes.

C · correct — IPv6 prefixes can be subdivided into subnets; the term overlaps the broad scheme wording.

D · correct — Classless prefix/CIDR terminology applies to flexible-prefix allocation and routing rather than historical class boundaries.

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET11 · Routers, gateways and traffic controls

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

Correct answer: A — To connect multiple networks together

The router definition explicitly interconnects LANs/WANs and determines next paths using routing tables. Firewall functionality may be added, but it is not the primary definition. Evidence: PDF 12, 11, 48.

Evidence in the complete study note

Routers forward IP packets between networks using destination prefixes and next hops. They separate broadcast domains and normally do not forward local link broadcasts. A default gateway is usually a router, while a protocol gateway can translate application formats; therefore a gateway is not inherently a device that implements every OSI layer.NET11
A firewall allows, rejects or inspects traffic under a security policy; it does not necessarily encrypt. A VPN, Virtual Private Network, provides a logical private connection over another network; a secure VPN authenticates/encrypts its tunnel. A modem modulates outgoing and demodulates incoming carrier signals. These functions may coexist in one home router but remain conceptually distinct.NET11
A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.NET09

B · incorrect — Signal regeneration is repeater work (PDF 12, 11, 48.)

D · incorrect — Bandwidth allocation is not the defining routing role (PDF 12, 11, 48.)

Question 190

Which OSI layer establishes and manages application dialogs, including checkpoints for recovery after an interruption?

  • A. Physical layer
  • B. Data Link layer
  • C. Transport layer
  • D. Session layer

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 494

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.

Study-guide sections

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

NET18 · Trace the TCP handshake

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

NET18 · Trace the TCP handshake

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

Correct answer: D — Session layer

Session-layer roles include establishing and managing dialogs and coordinating checkpoints so a transfer can resume after an interruption. TCP transport connections are a different form of connection state and do not make every reference to a dialog a transport function. Physical signaling and hop-local link delivery likewise have different scopes. The revised stem identifies dialog and checkpoint management as the lifecycle being classified.

Evidence in the complete study note

OSI session roles establish/manage dialogs and can coordinate checkpoints so transfer resumes after interruption. Presentation roles translate encodings and handle compression/encryption. Compression reduces representation size; encryption hides content and need not shrink it. Application protocols provide services directly to applications. Practical implementations distribute these functions differently; TLS is not proof of a separate physical presentation-layer device.NET19
TCP establishes state with SYN, SYN+ACK, then ACK. SYN consumes one sequence position even with no application bytes. An acknowledgment states the next expected sequence number. For client ISN=395 and server ISN=260: client sends SYN seq395; server sends SYN+ACK seq260 ack396; client sends ACK seq396 ack261. Later byte counts advance sequence numbers. FIN also consumes one sequence position.NET18
Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.NET14

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Physical signaling does not perform application-dialog management or checkpoint coordination.

B · incorrect — Data link handles hop-local frames and link procedures rather than application dialogs and checkpoints.

C · incorrect — Transport handles process delivery and TCP connection state, not the session-dialog role specified.

D · correct — Session manages dialogs and can coordinate checkpoints for recovery.

Evidence in the complete study note

TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.NET17
IP supplies connectionless best-effort packet delivery, not end-to-end ordering or retransmission. IPv4 addresses are 32 bits. Its minimum header is 20 bytes and can grow to 60 bytes; it is not a 32-bit header. IHL counts 32-bit words; total length includes header and payload. TTL limits lifetime across routers; the protocol field identifies TCP, UDP or another upper-layer protocol.NET16
HTTP defines web request/response semantics; it is stateless, and a message body may be absent. HTTPS adds TLS protection. FTP transfers files using control and separate data connections; it is not the same protocol as SFTP. SMTP submits and relays mail; POP3 retrieves messages and IMAP accesses/synchronizes server mailboxes. Saying SMTP handles both sending and end-user mailbox retrieval is inaccurate.NET21

Question 192

Which layer of the OSI reference model is responsible for addressing and routing data packets across different networks?

  • A. Network layer
  • B. Data Link layer
  • C. Transport layer
  • D. Physical layer

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 496

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.

Study-guide sections

NET30 · Routing algorithms and destination sets

NET12 · OSI layers and encapsulation

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET30 · Routing algorithms and destination sets

NET12 · OSI layers and encapsulation

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Correct answer: A — Network layer

Network explicitly adds logical addressing and routes packets from source to destination across intermediate devices. Evidence: PDF 15, 15, 16, 14.

Evidence in the complete study note

Routing computes paths; forwarding chooses a next hop for an individual packet. Select the matching route with the longest prefix, then apply the routing system’s tie-breaking criteria. A default /0 matches when nothing more specific does. Static routes are configured; dynamic protocols exchange reachability. Distance vector uses neighbor estimates, while link state distributes link information and computes shortest paths. Interior protocols operate within an autonomous system; BGP exchanges routes between systems.NET30
Sending proceeds from application data to transport segment/datagram, network packet, link frame and physical bits/symbols; receiving reverses the order. Each layer serves the layer above. A router removes a received link frame, inspects IP, and creates a new link frame for the next hop. MAC addresses usually change across routed hops; end-to-end IP addresses ordinarily remain until translation.NET12
Ports identify transport endpoints; the application can choose a transport and request socket buffer sizes, subject to OS limits. A TCP connection is identified by source/destination IP and source/destination port, with TCP understood. IPv4 protocol numbers identify upper protocols; 80 is a usual HTTP port, not an IP protocol number. Clients often use ephemeral ports. SCTP is a reliable message-oriented transport with multiple streams.NET17

B · incorrect — Data link handles physical addresses and one-hop frames (PDF 15, 15, 16, 14.)

C · incorrect — Transport delivers to processes with ports (PDF 15, 15, 16, 14.)

D · incorrect — Physical delivers bits/signals (PDF 15, 15, 16, 14.)

Question 193

Which OSI layer supplies hop-local frame acknowledgments and retransmission when a reliable-link protocol is used, rather than end-to-end transport recovery?

  • A. Network layer
  • B. Transport layer
  • C. Data Link layer
  • D. Application layer

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 497

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.

Study-guide sections

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

NET13 · Link control, framing and error detection

NET16 · Network delivery and IPv4 header

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

NET13 · Link control, framing and error detection

NET16 · Network delivery and IPv4 header

Correct answer: C — Data Link layer

Reliable data-link protocols can acknowledge frames and retransmit missing or damaged frames across a single hop. Transport recovery instead covers the end-to-end communication between processes. Network-layer IPv4 includes a header checksum but remains best-effort and does not supply this frame ARQ service. The link-layer role is protocol-dependent: Ethernet error detection alone does not guarantee reliable local delivery.

Evidence in the complete study note

Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.NET14
Detection adds redundancy but does not guarantee correction. Even parity adds a bit so the total number of ones is even: 1011 needs parity 1. It detects every odd number of bit flips but misses even counts. CRC treats bits as a polynomial and appends the XOR-division remainder; the receiver repeats the division. Internet checksums add words with end-around carry and complement the sum. A burst spans from the first corrupted bit through the last, including unchanged interior bits. Retransmission or sufficient forward-error-correcting redundancy is needed for recovery.NET13
The IPv4 checksum protects its header; IP does not lack error checking altogether. Identification, flags and offset support fragmentation. IPv4 sources and routers may fragment when allowed; reassembly occurs at the destination. If DF is set and the next MTU is too small, forwarding fails and an ICMP diagnostic may be returned.NET16

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — IP routing and its header checksum are not the requested hop-local frame ARQ service.

B · incorrect — Transport reliability has end-to-end rather than one-link scope.

C · correct — Data link implements the specified hop-local frame acknowledgment/retransmission procedure.

D · incorrect — Application services are above the specified link-frame recovery mechanism.

FTP transfers files using control and separate data connections; it is not the same protocol as SFTP. SMTP submits and relays mail; POP3 retrieves messages and IMAP accesses/synchronizes server mailboxes. Saying SMTP handles both sending and end-user mailbox retrieval is inaccurate.NET21
DNS resolves names to records, including IPv4 A and IPv6 AAAA addresses; it can use UDP or TCP port 53. DHCP dynamically leases IPv4 settings, commonly address, mask, gateway and DNS server. Its basic exchange is discover, offer, request, acknowledge. IP itself does not assign addresses.NET20

Choice by choice

A · correct — SMTP submits and relays mail, including server acceptance of incoming messages.

B · incorrect — FTP transfers files through a separate protocol rather than the mail flow defined here.

C · incorrect — HTTP defines web request/response exchanges rather than the mail submission and relay protocol requested.

D · incorrect — DNS supplies records such as mail-exchanger names rather than delivering or retrieving message contents.

Question 195

Which layer of the OSI reference model is responsible for converting data into a format suitable for transmission over a network?

  • A. Presentation layer
  • B. Session layer
  • C. Physical layer
  • D. Application layer

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 499

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.

Study-guide sections

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

Correct answer: A — Presentation layer for representation/format translation

The word format identifies representation translation rather than routing or connection management. NET19 assigns encoding translation and other representation work to presentation. Physical signaling maps bits to medium symbols, but does not supply the application-data format translation asked for. Thus A matches the intended formatting responsibility.

Evidence in the complete study note

OSI session roles establish/manage dialogs and can coordinate checkpoints so transfer resumes after interruption. Presentation roles translate encodings and handle compression/encryption. Compression reduces representation size; encryption hides content and need not shrink it. Application protocols provide services directly to applications. Practical implementations distribute these functions differently; TLS is not proof of a separate physical presentation-layer device.NET19
A NIC supplies a computer’s network interface and commonly implements both physical and link functions. Calling a NIC a physical interface does not mean all its functions are layer 1. Physical specifications include connectors, signaling, voltage, timing and physical coding/modulation; the PHY interface to MAC handles hardware signaling.NET09

Choice by choice

A · correct — Presentation translates representations/encodings into suitable data formats.

B · incorrect — Session manages dialogs and checkpoints rather than data representation formats.

C · incorrect — Physical maps bits/symbols to signals, a different responsibility from representation-format translation.

D · incorrect — Application supplies network services to applications rather than the distinct presentation-format function.

Question 197

Which layer of the OSI reference model is responsible for establishing and terminating sessions between applications?

  • A. Presentation layer
  • B. Session layer
  • C. Transport layer
  • D. Application layer

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 501

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.

Study-guide sections

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

NET18 · Trace the TCP handshake

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

NET18 · Trace the TCP handshake

Correct answer: B — Session layer

The session layer establishes communication dialogs and controls/synchronizes their interaction, matching the explicitly stated sessions between applications. Evidence: PDF 16, 16, 16, 16.

Evidence in the complete study note

OSI session roles establish/manage dialogs and can coordinate checkpoints so transfer resumes after interruption. Presentation roles translate encodings and handle compression/encryption. Compression reduces representation size; encryption hides content and need not shrink it. Application protocols provide services directly to applications. Practical implementations distribute these functions differently; TLS is not proof of a separate physical presentation-layer device.NET19
TCP establishes state with SYN, SYN+ACK, then ACK. SYN consumes one sequence position even with no application bytes. An acknowledgment states the next expected sequence number. For client ISN=395 and server ISN=260: client sends SYN seq395; server sends SYN+ACK seq260 ack396; client sends ACK seq396 ack261. Later byte counts advance sequence numbers. FIN also consumes one sequence position.NET18

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Presentation performs representation translation (PDF 16, 16, 16, 16.)

B · correct — Session establishes and synchronizes dialogs (PDF 16, 16, 16, 16.)

C · incorrect — Transport connection setup is a different scope from the stated application sessions (PDF 16, 16, 16, 16.)

D · incorrect — Application provides user access to network services (PDF 16, 16, 16, 16.)

Question 198

A file-transfer client uses one connection for protocol commands and a separate connection for file data. Which listed application protocol uses this control/data separation?

  • A. SMTP
  • B. HTTP
  • C. FTP
  • D. TCP

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 502

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify the requested service or delivery guarantee, then distinguish application roles, transport behavior and address configuration.

Study-guide sections

NET21 · Web, file, mail and remote-login protocols

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET21 · Web, file, mail and remote-login protocols

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Correct answer: C — FTP

FTP separates its control conversation from the data connection used for transfers. That architectural feature distinguishes it from the broad ability to download files, which HTTP also provides. SMTP handles mail submission and relay. TCP is the transport service on which an application protocol can build connections; it does not itself define FTP commands or the application’s separate control and data roles.

Evidence in the complete study note

HTTP defines web request/response semantics; it is stateless, and a message body may be absent. HTTPS adds TLS protection. FTP transfers files using control and separate data connections; it is not the same protocol as SFTP. SMTP submits and relays mail; POP3 retrieves messages and IMAP accesses/synchronizes server mailboxes. Saying SMTP handles both sending and end-user mailbox retrieval is inaccurate.NET21
TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.NET17

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — SMTP defines mail transfer, not the described FTP control/data arrangement.

B · incorrect — HTTP can transfer files, but does not define the described separate FTP control and data connections.

C · correct — FTP uses separate control and data connections.

D · incorrect — TCP provides transport connections; the application protocol defines their command/data roles.
