NET20 · DNS, DHCP and address resolution

NET21 · Web, file, mail and remote-login protocols

Correct answer: D — DNS

DNS is the name-resolution application protocol in NET20. A/AAAA records provide address data for names. SMTP submits/relays mail, FTP transfers files and HTTP serves web requests; none provides the requested general domain-name record service. Its lookup role is separate from DHCP address assignment.

Evidence in the complete study note

DNS resolves names to records, including IPv4 A and IPv6 AAAA addresses; it can use UDP or TCP port 53. DHCP dynamically leases IPv4 settings, commonly address, mask, gateway and DNS server. Its basic exchange is discover, offer, request, acknowledge. IP itself does not assign addresses.NET20
HTTP defines web request/response semantics; it is stateless, and a message body may be absent. HTTPS adds TLS protection. FTP transfers files using control and separate data connections; it is not the same protocol as SFTP. SMTP submits and relays mail; POP3 retrieves messages and IMAP accesses/synchronizes server mailboxes. Saying SMTP handles both sending and end-user mailbox retrieval is inaccurate.NET21

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — SMTP submits and relays mail rather than resolving hostnames to addresses.

B · incorrect — FTP transfers files and does not supply the name-resolution record service.

C · incorrect — HTTP defines web exchanges, not the general hostname-to-address service.

D · correct — DNS resolves names into records such as A and AAAA address records.

Question 240

Crosstalk is best described as:

  • A. Loss of signal strength over distance
  • B. Signals from one communication channel leaking into an adjacent channel
  • C. Random electron motion causing electrical noise
  • D. Delay caused by varying signal frequencies

Source

  • Data Communication & Networking review questions · Question 16

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Compare the signal mechanism, medium properties or transmission direction against the definitions and stated physical assumptions.

Study-guide sections

NET06 · Delay, impairments and transmission modes

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET06 · Delay, impairments and transmission modes

Correct answer: B — Leakage from an adjacent communication channel

Crosstalk is unwanted coupling from a neighboring communication channel, directly matching B. Strength loss is attenuation, random thermal motion creates thermal noise and differential frequency delay produces distortion. These impairments can coexist but their definitions are distinct, so the question’s mechanism identifies crosstalk specifically.

Evidence in the complete study note

Attenuation reduces signal strength. Distortion changes shape, often because frequencies have different delays. Noise adds unwanted energy: thermal noise comes from random thermal motion, crosstalk leaks from nearby channels, and impulse noise is a short disturbance. Amplifiers amplify noise too; digital repeaters regenerate decisions but cannot reconstruct every corrupted bit.NET06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Signal-strength loss is attenuation rather than coupling from a neighboring channel.

B · correct — Signals leaking into an adjacent channel are crosstalk.

C · incorrect — Random electron/thermal motion describes thermal noise.

D · incorrect — Different component-frequency delays distort waveform shape rather than defining crosstalk.

Question 241

How many usable host addresses are available in the subnet 192.168.2.64/26?

  • A. 32
  • B. 64
  • C. 62
  • D. 30

Source

  • Data Communication & Networking review questions · Question 17

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule.

Study-guide sections

NET25 · Find subnet bounds and usable hosts

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET25 · Find subnet bounds and usable hosts

Correct answer: C — 62 usable hosts

A /26 leaves six host bits, so the block has 64 addresses. In the specified block, .64 is the network and .127 the broadcast; usable hosts span .65–.126 inclusive, totaling 62. The question asks usable hosts, not block size, and /31 point-to-point exceptions do not apply.

Evidence in the complete study note

For ordinary broadcast LANs let h=32-p. Total addresses=2^h; usable hosts=2^h-2, reserving network and directed broadcast. Find the changing octet’s increment as 256-mask octet, round the address down to a multiple, and extend through the next boundary minus one.NET25
192.168.2.64/26 spans .64–.127; usable .65–.126 gives 62 hosts. 192.168.10.25/28 spans .16–.31, so its network is .16. 172.17.128.0/21 spans 172.17.128.0–172.17.135.255; .128.255 and .135.0 are valid interior hosts, but .135.255 is broadcast. /27 gives 32 total and 30 usable, not 32 usable.NET25

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Thirty-two is not the usable count of this /26 block; /26 has 64 total addresses.

B · incorrect — Sixty-four is the total block size before network/broadcast reservations.

C · correct — Six host bits give 64 total addresses minus two reservations, leaving 62 usable hosts.

D · incorrect — Thirty usable hosts is the /27 result, not /26.

Question 242

Which OSI layer is responsible for establishing, maintaining, and ending communication sessions?

  • A. Transport Layer
  • B. Session Layer
  • C. Application Layer
  • D. Presentation Layer

Source

  • Data Communication & Networking review questions · Question 18

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.

Study-guide sections

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

NET18 · Trace the TCP handshake

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

NET18 · Trace the TCP handshake

Correct answer: B — Session layer

The stem explicitly specifies communication sessions, matching the OSI session role rather than merely a TCP connection. NET19 assigns dialog management and checkpoints to that layer. Transport serves process endpoints, application supplies services and presentation handles representations. B is therefore the specific reference-model lifecycle role.

Evidence in the complete study note

OSI session roles establish/manage dialogs and can coordinate checkpoints so transfer resumes after interruption. Presentation roles translate encodings and handle compression/encryption. Compression reduces representation size; encryption hides content and need not shrink it. Application protocols provide services directly to applications. Practical implementations distribute these functions differently; TLS is not proof of a separate physical presentation-layer device.NET19
TCP establishes state with SYN, SYN+ACK, then ACK. SYN consumes one sequence position even with no application bytes. An acknowledgment states the next expected sequence number. For client ISN=395 and server ISN=260: client sends SYN seq395; server sends SYN+ACK seq260 ack396; client sends ACK seq396 ack261. Later byte counts advance sequence numbers. FIN also consumes one sequence position.NET18

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Transport connection state is distinct from the explicitly named OSI session/dialog lifecycle.

B · correct — Session manages dialogs and their setup, maintenance and recovery/end lifecycle.

C · incorrect — Application supplies user/application network services rather than the distinct session-layer lifecycle.

D · incorrect — Presentation translates/compresses/encrypts representations instead of managing dialogs.

Question 243

A bus topology network has 20 nodes. If the main cable breaks, what happens?

  • A. Only the two nodes nearest the break are affected
  • B. The network continues to function normally
  • C. The entire network goes down
  • D. Only the node that caused the break is disconnected

Source

  • Data Communication & Networking review questions · Question 19

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Draw the links and identify shared components, alternate paths and the effect of the specified failure or growth requirement.

Study-guide sections

NET08 · Topology and failure reasoning

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET08 · Topology and failure reasoning

Correct answer: C — A main-backbone break can disrupt the whole basic bus segment

In the conventional single-backbone bus assumed by these options, a main-cable break disrupts the shared segment, affecting the network rather than just one endpoint. NET08 qualifies the physical mechanism as an unterminated break. Redundant segmentation or protected designs are not specified, so C expresses the standard basic-bus failure consequence.

Evidence in the complete study note

Bus uses a shared backbone; an unterminated break can disrupt the segment. Star connects endpoints through a central device: one edge failure isolates that endpoint, whereas central failure affects the star. Ring forms a loop; basic single rings are vulnerable to a break, while protected dual rings differ. Token passing is associated with Token Ring but is an access method, not a necessary property of every ring. Tree is hierarchical; hybrid combines arrangements.NET08

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — A main-backbone fault affects shared signaling, not merely the two closest nodes.

B · incorrect — A broken unterminated backbone does not preserve normal basic-bus operation.

C · correct — The shared basic bus segment can fail as a whole when its main backbone is broken.

D · incorrect — A backbone break differs from an isolated endpoint spur failure and need not be limited to one node.

Question 244

Synchronous data transmission differs from asynchronous in that synchronous transmission:

  • A. Uses start and stop bits for each data chunk
  • B. Sends data continuously with sender and receiver using the same clock
  • C. Is always slower than asynchronous
  • D. Cannot transmit binary data

Source

  • Data Communication & Networking review questions · Question 20

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule.

Study-guide sections

NET06 · Delay, impairments and transmission modes

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET06 · Delay, impairments and transmission modes

Correct answer: B — Ongoing synchronized clock recovery rather than per-character start/stop

NET06 contrasts character start/stop framing with ongoing clock recovery in synchronous transmission. B is the intended synchronized-transfer description; “same clock” should mean synchronized timing, not necessarily a single physical clock device. The note gives no universal speed ordering, and both methods can transmit digital/binary data.

Evidence in the complete study note

Simplex is one way, half duplex alternates directions, and full duplex permits simultaneous sending/receiving. A walkie-talkie is half duplex; a telephone conversation uses full duplex. Serial sends sequential bits; parallel uses multiple conductors and may suffer skew. Character-oriented asynchronous serial adds start/stop bits; synchronous framing uses ongoing clock recovery. Neither is synonymous with browser asynchronous requests.NET06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Per-character start/stop bits describe character-oriented asynchronous serial transmission.

B · correct — Synchronous transfer maintains coordinated timing through ongoing clock recovery rather than character start/stop framing.

C · incorrect — No universal slower-than-asynchronous rule follows from the timing method.

D · incorrect — Synchronous framing can carry binary data; the timing convention does not prohibit it.

Question 245

What is the PRIMARY function of the Network Layer (Layer 3)?

  • A. Providing physical transmission of bits
  • B. Error detection and MAC addressing
  • C. End-to-end routing of data between different networks using IP addresses
  • D. Establishing communication sessions between applications

Source

  • Data Communication & Networking review questions · Question 21

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.

Study-guide sections

NET11 · Routers, gateways and traffic controls

NET12 · OSI layers and encapsulation

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET11 · Routers, gateways and traffic controls

NET12 · OSI layers and encapsulation

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

Correct answer: C — Logical IP addressing and routing across networks

NET12 gives network-layer logical addressing and routing; NET11 explains forwarding IP packets among networks by destination prefixes. C directly states that responsibility. The other options assign physical signaling, link MAC/error detection and session-dialog management, which belong to different model layers.

Evidence in the complete study note

Routers forward IP packets between networks using destination prefixes and next hops. They separate broadcast domains and normally do not forward local link broadcasts. A default gateway is usually a router, while a protocol gateway can translate application formats; therefore a gateway is not inherently a device that implements every OSI layer.NET11
Sending proceeds from application data to transport segment/datagram, network packet, link frame and physical bits/symbols; receiving reverses the order. Each layer serves the layer above. A router removes a received link frame, inspects IP, and creates a new link frame for the next hop. MAC addresses usually change across routed hops; end-to-end IP addresses ordinarily remain until translation.NET12
OSI session roles establish/manage dialogs and can coordinate checkpoints so transfer resumes after interruption. Presentation roles translate encodings and handle compression/encryption. Compression reduces representation size; encryption hides content and need not shrink it. Application protocols provide services directly to applications. Practical implementations distribute these functions differently; TLS is not proof of a separate physical presentation-layer device.NET19

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Transporting raw physical bits/symbols is the physical-layer function.

B · incorrect — MAC addressing and hop frame error detection are data-link responsibilities.

C · correct — Network-layer logical addressing and routing carry IP packets between networks.

D · incorrect — Establishing application dialogs is a session-layer role rather than IP routing.

Question 246

Which of the following IPv4 addresses is INVALID?

  • A. 192.168.0.1
  • B. 10.0.0.255
  • C. 172.16.254.1
  • D. 10.256.0.1

Source

  • Data Communication & Networking review questions · Question 22

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate address width, syntax, reserved scope and the supplied prefix or historical classful convention.

Study-guide sections

NET22 · IPv4 notation and classful defaults

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET22 · IPv4 notation and classful defaults

Correct answer: D — 10.256.0.1 has an impossible octet

An IPv4 decimal octet must fit eight bits, from 0 through 255. D has 256 and is therefore syntactically invalid. A–C each meet that range condition. B’s .255 ending alone does not establish a broadcast without a prefix, so it cannot be rejected merely by its last octet.

Evidence in the complete study note

Write IPv4 as four decimal octets 0–255, or as 32 binary bits. Use weights 128,64,32,16,8,4,2,1 within each octet. Thus 11000001 10000011 00011011 11111111 is 193.131.27.255. A value such as 257 is impossible. Syntactic validity differs from assignability: an address ending .0 or .255 can be a host under some prefixes.NET22

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — All four octets are within 0–255, so this notation is valid.

B · incorrect — Every octet is valid; a .255 ending alone does not determine broadcast status without a prefix.

C · incorrect — All four values fit eight-bit octets and form valid dotted-decimal notation.

D · correct — The second octet 256 exceeds the maximum representable eight-bit value 255.

Question 247

In IPv6, addresses are how many bits long?

  • A. 32 bits
  • B. 64 bits
  • C. 96 bits
  • D. 128 bits

Source

  • Data Communication & Networking review questions · Question 23

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate address width, syntax, reserved scope and the supplied prefix or historical classful convention.

Study-guide sections

NET23 · Special ranges, private addresses and IPv6

NET16 · Network delivery and IPv4 header

NET-S06 · Interface addresses and transport-number namespaces

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET23 · Special ranges, private addresses and IPv6

NET16 · Network delivery and IPv4 header

NET-S06 · Interface addresses and transport-number namespaces

Correct answer: D — 128 bits

NET23 explicitly gives IPv6 addresses a 128-bit width. IPv4 uses 32 bits; 64 may describe a common subnet interface boundary but is not the whole IPv6 address length. Ninety-six bits is likewise not the full width. D therefore answers the requested address size.

Evidence in the complete study note

IPv6 has 128-bit hexadecimal addresses, flexible prefixes and no IPv4-style broadcast. Sources, not routers, fragment IPv6 packets. IPv6 does not automatically encrypt traffic or make authentication unnecessary. Compare IPv6’s larger 128-bit address space and encryption support separately; specify the property being evaluated.NET23
IP supplies connectionless best-effort packet delivery, not end-to-end ordering or retransmission. IPv4 addresses are 32 bits. Its minimum header is 20 bytes and can grow to 60 bytes; it is not a 32-bit header. IHL counts 32-bit words; total length includes header and payload. TTL limits lifetime across routers; the protocol field identifies TCP, UDP or another upper-layer protocol.NET16
A common IPv6 unicast subnet uses a 64-bit subnet prefix and a 64-bit interface identifier. This split does not make the complete address 64 bits: it remains 128 bits. Special uses and explicitly different prefix lengths must be considered separately.NET-S06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Thirty-two bits is the IPv4 address width, not IPv6.

B · incorrect — Sixty-four bits is not the complete IPv6 address width.

C · incorrect — Ninety-six bits does not match the specified 128-bit IPv6 address length.

D · correct — IPv6 addresses contain 128 bits as explicitly stated in NET23.

Question 248

A bridge decides whether to forward a frame to another network segment by examining the:

  • A. IP address in the packet header
  • B. Port number in the segment header
  • C. Source and destination MAC addresses
  • D. TTL (Time to Live) field

Source

  • Data Communication & Networking review questions · Question 24

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions.

Study-guide sections

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

NET16 · Network delivery and IPv4 header

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

NET16 · Network delivery and IPv4 header

Correct answer: C — Learn source MACs and forward according to destination MAC

A bridge learns which sources are reachable through each port and consults the destination MAC when forwarding/filtering a frame. C names the relevant link addresses. IP, transport ports and TTL belong to higher-layer packet/segment processing, not the ordinary bridge forwarding decision. Unknown destinations may be flooded, so learning does not imply always-one-port forwarding.

Evidence in the complete study note

A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.NET10
Ports identify transport endpoints; the application can choose a transport and request socket buffer sizes, subject to OS limits. A TCP connection is identified by source/destination IP and source/destination port, with TCP understood. IPv4 protocol numbers identify upper protocols; 80 is a usual HTTP port, not an IP protocol number. Clients often use ephemeral ports. SCTP is a reliable message-oriented transport with multiple streams.NET17
IP supplies connectionless best-effort packet delivery, not end-to-end ordering or retransmission. IPv4 addresses are 32 bits. Its minimum header is 20 bytes and can grow to 60 bytes; it is not a 32-bit header. IHL counts 32-bit words; total length includes header and payload. TTL limits lifetime across routers; the protocol field identifies TCP, UDP or another upper-layer protocol.NET16

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Destination IP prefixes drive routing, not ordinary layer-2 bridge frame forwarding.

B · incorrect — Transport ports identify process endpoints and are not the bridge MAC-table lookup key.

C · correct — Source MAC informs learning and destination MAC informs forwarding/filtering to the appropriate segment.

D · incorrect — TTL is an IP header field used in routed packet lifetime, not ordinary bridging.

Question 249

Circuit switching guarantees bandwidth for the duration of a call. What is the main DISADVANTAGE of this?

  • A. High latency during transmission
  • B. Bandwidth is wasted when no data is actively being transmitted
  • C. Packets may arrive out of order
  • D. It cannot support voice communication

Source

  • Data Communication & Networking review questions · Question 25

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions.

Study-guide sections

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

Correct answer: B — Reserved bandwidth can be wasted during silence

Circuit switching holds resources for the call even while endpoints are silent, so unused reservation cannot be statistically shared as packet traffic would be. B gives that cost. Circuit switching does not inherently deliver packets out of order or prevent voice transmission; traditional telephone calls are a standard example.

Evidence in the complete study note

Circuit switching sets up a path with reserved resources, transfers data, then releases it. Predictable allocated bandwidth trades against setup/blocking and wasted reservation during silence. A traditional telephone call is the standard example. Packet switching divides data into packets that share links statistically; queueing can add variable delay and loss. This does not make modern voice-over-packet impossible: buffering, scheduling and capacity planning manage it.NET31

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Reserved circuits can offer predictable transfer behavior; setup cost is distinct from universally high transfer latency.

B · correct — Capacity remains reserved during silence and can be wasted when no data is sent.

C · incorrect — Independent out-of-order packet routing is not the defining reserved-circuit disadvantage.

D · incorrect — Traditional telephone calls are the note’s standard circuit-switching example, so voice is supported.

Question 250

Under the textbook direct line-of-sight wireless-link convention, which option gives the most complete set of listed technologies whose direct path can be blocked by buildings or terrain? Treat radio waves as the broad category rather than assuming every radio propagation mode needs line of sight.

  • A. Radio waves
  • B. Microwaves
  • C. Infrared
  • D. Both B and C

Adapted from

  • Data Communication & Networking review questions · Question 26

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Compare the signal mechanism, medium properties or transmission direction against the definitions and stated physical assumptions.

Study-guide sections

NET07 · Cables, wireless and connectors

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET07 · Cables, wireless and connectors

Correct answer: D — Microwave and infrared under the conventional line-of-sight assumption

Conventional directional microwave links need suitable path visibility, and infrared generally does not penetrate walls. Obstacles can therefore interrupt the direct links specified here. Both individual technologies fit, so the combined option is the complete response. Radio waves is a broader physical category that includes microwave but also other propagation modes; the question does not assert that all radio links share the same line-of-sight restriction.

Evidence in the complete study note

Radio, microwave and infrared are unguided media. Ground waves follow Earth, sky waves can reflect from ionized layers, and line-of-sight paths require suitable visibility. Microwaves are radio waves in the broader physical classification. Infrared generally does not penetrate walls. Directionality depends on antennas: omnidirectional means broad azimuth coverage, not equal radiation in every 3-D direction. Legacy Ethernet straight-through cables join unlike MDI/MDI-X roles; crossover joins like roles, such as PC–PC or switch–switch. Auto-MDI-X can remove that requirement.NET07

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — The broad radio category includes propagation modes beyond the specified line-of-sight comparison.

B · incorrect — Microwave fits the stated direct-link case, but this alone omits infrared.

C · incorrect — Infrared fits the stated obstructed-direct-path case, but this alone omits microwave.

D · correct — Both microwave and infrared fit the specified comparison, making this the complete set.

Question 251

What does CIDR stand for, and what problem did it solve?

  • A. Classless Inter-Domain Routing; it solved address wastage in classful addressing
  • B. Classful Internet Domain Routing; it solved packet loss
  • C. Centralized IP Domain Routing; it solved routing loops
  • D. Classless Internet Data Routing; it solved latency in WANs

Apply the cited definitions to the stated scope; for calculations, derive the result from the supplied prefix, bit count or resource rule.

Study-guide sections

NET28 · Point-to-point links and route aggregation

NET26 · Borrow bits and choose a mask

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET28 · Point-to-point links and route aggregation

NET26 · Borrow bits and choose a mask

Correct answer: A — Classless Inter-Domain Routing; flexible prefixes reduce rigid class allocation waste

CIDR replaces rigid class allocation. Flexible prefixes allow blocks sized to requirements and aggregation of aligned blocks, addressing waste from fixed historical class sizes. The other expansions are incorrect and their proposed packet-loss, loop or latency cures are not the defined purpose.

Evidence in the complete study note

CIDR, Classless Inter-Domain Routing, replaces rigid class allocation and supports aggregation. Combine contiguous aligned blocks sharing leading bits; unrelated adjacent-looking labels may not aggregate cleanly. Four consecutive /26 blocks covering a /24 summarize to /24. More-specific routes must remain available where the aggregate would otherwise send traffic to the wrong next hop.NET28
For H hosts, choose the smallest h satisfying 2^h-2≥H, then p=32-h. For 24 hosts use /27; 52 or 57 use /26; 100 use /25; 500 use /23. For at least six equal subnets choose b=3. A Class C /24 split to /27 yields eight subnets. Always check both the number of subnets and the host capacity.NET26

A · correct — This gives the correct expansion and relates flexible prefix allocation to avoiding rigid class-size waste.

B · incorrect — Classful Internet Domain Routing is the wrong expansion, and CIDR is not defined as a packet-loss cure.

C · incorrect — Centralized IP Domain Routing is not the acronym expansion or the stated mechanism.

D · incorrect — Classless Internet Data Routing is incorrect; CIDR is not defined as a general WAN-latency cure.

NET26 · Borrow bits and choose a mask

Correct answer: C — 32 subnets

Borrowing five bits yields 2^5=32 equal subnets under modern counting. The parent Class B /16 would become /21, but the direct subnet count only needs the specified five borrowed bits. NET26 says not to subtract two subnets under modern practice.

Study-guide sections

NET08 · Topology and failure reasoning

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET08 · Topology and failure reasoning

Correct answer: B — The dependent star loses connectivity when its center fails

In a basic star every endpoint depends on the central hub for communication with other endpoints. Failure of that common center therefore affects the whole star. No alternate center or automatic topology reconfiguration is specified; the network does not become a bus or ring merely because the hub stops functioning.

Evidence in the complete study note

Bus uses a shared backbone; an unterminated break can disrupt the segment. Star connects endpoints through a central device: one edge failure isolates that endpoint, whereas central failure affects the star. Ring forms a loop; basic single rings are vulnerable to a break, while protected dual rings differ. Token passing is associated with Token Ring but is an access method, not a necessary property of every ring. Tree is hierarchical; hybrid combines arrangements.NET08

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — The center serves all star endpoints, so its failure is not limited to the nearest neighbor.

B · correct — All endpoints depend on the central hub, so the basic star loses inter-endpoint connectivity.

C · incorrect — A hub failure does not physically or logically rewire the star into an operational bus.

D · incorrect — No automatic ring reconnection mechanism follows from the basic star topology.

Question 256

What type of noise CANNOT be completely eliminated because it is caused by the random motion of electrons due to temperature?

  • A. Crosstalk
  • B. Impulse noise
  • C. Thermal noise
  • D. Intermodulation noise

Apply the cited definitions to the stated scope; for calculations, derive the result from the supplied prefix, bit count or resource rule.

Study-guide sections

NET06 · Delay, impairments and transmission modes

NET-S07 · Physical signaling and legacy Ethernet cable roles

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET06 · Delay, impairments and transmission modes

NET-S07 · Physical signaling and legacy Ethernet cable roles

Correct answer: C — Thermal noise

The stated cause—random motion associated with temperature—is thermal noise in NET06. Crosstalk is neighboring-channel coupling and impulse noise is a short disturbance. D names a different noise phenomenon not defined by random thermal motion. The cause identifies C without requiring a claim that all other real noise can be perfectly eliminated.

Evidence in the complete study note

Attenuation reduces signal strength. Distortion changes shape, often because frequencies have different delays. Noise adds unwanted energy: thermal noise comes from random thermal motion, crosstalk leaks from nearby channels, and impulse noise is a short disturbance. Amplifiers amplify noise too; digital repeaters regenerate decisions but cannot reconstruct every corrupted bit.NET06
Intermodulation distortion occurs when multiple signals interact through a nonlinear component and generate unwanted combination-frequency products. Its mechanism differs from random thermal motion, adjacent-channel leakage and an isolated impulse disturbance.NET-S07

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Crosstalk arises from coupling between nearby communication channels, not the stated thermal-motion cause.

B · incorrect — Impulse noise is a short disturbance rather than persistent random thermal motion.

C · correct — Thermal noise is explicitly caused by random thermal motion, matching the temperature-dependent clue.

D · incorrect — This option does not match the random thermal-motion definition supplied in NET06.

Question 260

Parallel data transmission sends multiple bits simultaneously. Its key DISADVANTAGE compared to serial transmission is:

  • A. It is always slower
  • B. It cannot be used for digital data
  • C. It requires more transmission lines and can suffer from interference between lines
  • D. It only works over fiber-optic cable

Study-guide sections

NET06 · Delay, impairments and transmission modes

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET06 · Delay, impairments and transmission modes

Correct answer: C — More conductors and interline impairments

Parallel transfer needs several conductors to carry simultaneous bits. Those paths can experience skew and neighboring-channel coupling, as NET06’s impairment definitions explain. C states the extra-line and interference burden. No universal slower-speed claim, inability to carry digital data or fiber-only restriction follows from parallel transmission.

Evidence in the complete study note

Simplex is one way, half duplex alternates directions, and full duplex permits simultaneous sending/receiving. A walkie-talkie is half duplex; a telephone conversation uses full duplex. Serial sends sequential bits; parallel uses multiple conductors and may suffer skew. Character-oriented asynchronous serial adds start/stop bits; synchronous framing uses ongoing clock recovery. Neither is synonymous with browser asynchronous requests.NET06
Attenuation reduces signal strength. Distortion changes shape, often because frequencies have different delays. Noise adds unwanted energy: thermal noise comes from random thermal motion, crosstalk leaks from nearby channels, and impulse noise is a short disturbance. Amplifiers amplify noise too; digital repeaters regenerate decisions but cannot reconstruct every corrupted bit.NET06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Parallel is not universally slower; performance depends on implementation, distance and synchronization.

B · incorrect — Parallel transmission can carry digital bits simultaneously, exactly as the stem states.

C · correct — Multiple conductors add wiring and can suffer skew or coupled interference between adjacent lines.

D · incorrect — Parallel transmission is not restricted to fiber and commonly concerns multiple electrical conductors.

Question 261

A packet-switching network may be UNSUITABLE for real-time voice communication because:

  • A. It requires a dedicated circuit
  • B. Variable latency and possible packet loss can disrupt real-time audio
  • C. It cannot carry voice signals
  • D. All bandwidth is reserved, leaving none for voice

Source

  • Data Communication & Networking review questions · Question 37

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Apply the cited definitions to the stated scope; for calculations, derive the result from the supplied prefix, bit count or resource rule.

Study-guide sections

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET31 · Circuit, message and packet switching

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

Correct answer: B — Variable delay and packet loss can disturb real-time audio

Real-time audio is sensitive to late or missing data. Packet networks may introduce variable queueing delay and loss, so B gives a plausible suitability issue. Modern voice over packets remains possible with buffering, scheduling and capacity planning; it is not intrinsically prohibited or dependent on reserved circuits.

Evidence in the complete study note

Circuit switching sets up a path with reserved resources, transfers data, then releases it. Predictable allocated bandwidth trades against setup/blocking and wasted reservation during silence. A traditional telephone call is the standard example. Packet switching divides data into packets that share links statistically; queueing can add variable delay and loss. This does not make modern voice-over-packet impossible: buffering, scheduling and capacity planning manage it.NET31
TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.NET17

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Datagram packet switching does not require a dedicated circuit before every communication.

B · correct — Variable queueing latency and loss can make audio arrive late or incomplete.

C · incorrect — NET31 explicitly allows voice over packets with suitable engineering.

D · incorrect — Statistical link sharing differs from reserving all bandwidth for established circuits.

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET25 · Find subnet bounds and usable hosts

Correct answer: B — 30 usable hosts

A /27 leaves five host bits regardless of the historical class of its parent. Those bits provide 32 total addresses. On an ordinary broadcast subnet, network and broadcast reserve two, leaving 30 usable host addresses. Parent classification matters for subnet counting, not this explicit-prefix host calculation.

Evidence in the complete study note

For ordinary broadcast LANs let h=32-p. Total addresses=2^h; usable hosts=2^h-2, reserving network and directed broadcast. Find the changing octet’s increment as 256-mask octet, round the address down to a multiple, and extend through the next boundary minus one.NET25

B · correct — Five host bits give 32−2=30 ordinary usable hosts.

NET30 · Routing algorithms and destination sets

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET30 · Routing algorithms and destination sets

Correct answer: D — Anycast

Anycast routes to one member of a set sharing the address, typically the nearest by routing metrics. That is not necessarily geographic distance. Multicast targets a subscribed group, broadcast all in scope and ordinary unicast a single designated destination. D uniquely matches the shared-address nearest-member rule.

Evidence in the complete study note

Flooding sends copies on eligible outgoing links with duplicate/lifetime controls; random walk picks a neighbor probabilistically. Unicast targets one destination, broadcast all in a scope, multicast a subscribed group and anycast one member sharing an address, normally nearest under routing metrics. B · incorrect — Broadcast targets all destinations within its scope, not the nearest member.

C · incorrect — Ordinary unicast targets one designated destination without the shared-address nearest-member semantics.

D · correct — Anycast selects one shared-address member, normally nearest according to routing metrics.

Question 265

Which option best describes a protocol-translating gateway joining unlike networked systems?

  • A. A device that boosts signal strength over long distances
  • B. A device that connects networks using the same protocol
  • C. A device that connects two or more networks using different protocols, topologies, or architectures
  • D. A device that filters traffic based on MAC addresses

Adapted from

  • Data Communication & Networking review questions · Question 41

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Apply the cited definitions to the stated scope; for calculations, derive the result from the supplied prefix, bit count or resource rule.

Study-guide sections

NET11 · Routers, gateways and traffic controls

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET11 · Routers, gateways and traffic controls

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

Correct answer: C — A device that connects two or more networks using different protocols, topologies, or architectures

Gateway has several networking meanings. A default IP gateway is commonly a router, while a protocol gateway translates between unlike protocols or application formats. The question asks for that translating role, so the option joining unlike systems fits. Signal regeneration belongs to repeaters, same-protocol routing does not require translation, and MAC-based filtering describes bridging or switching rather than protocol conversion.

Evidence in the complete study note

Routers forward IP packets between networks using destination prefixes and next hops. They separate broadcast domains and normally do not forward local link broadcasts. A default gateway is usually a router, while a protocol gateway can translate application formats; therefore a gateway is not inherently a device that implements every OSI layer.NET11
A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.NET10
A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.NET09

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Signal regeneration/strength extension is a repeater function rather than either gateway meaning defined here.

B · incorrect — Connecting networks using the same protocol describes routing without the required protocol translation.

C · correct — A protocol gateway joins unlike systems through the translation required by the stated scope.

D · incorrect — MAC-address frame filtering describes bridging/switching rather than the gateway distinction in NET11.

  • B. 10.200.0.0
  • C. 10.200.240.0
  • D. 0.0.0.0

NET22 · IPv4 notation and classful defaults

NET24 · Masks, prefixes and binary AND

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET22 · IPv4 notation and classful defaults

NET24 · Masks, prefixes and binary AND

Correct answer: A — 10.0.0.0 under the explicitly requested Class A default

Because the question explicitly assigns Class A, its historical default /8 supplies the intended network/host boundary. Keep first octet 10 and zero the remaining 24 host bits to obtain 10.0.0.0. If a different CIDR prefix were supplied it would override the default, but none is given in this class-specific question.

Evidence in the complete study note

Historical classes use leading patterns: A 0 with /8, B 10 with /16, C 110 with /24; D 1110 is multicast and E 1111 reserved. Ordinary class-A first octets are 1–126 because 0 and 127 have special uses. B spans 128–191 and C 192–223. Default usable counts are 2^24-2, 2^16-2 and 254. Modern CIDR requires the actual prefix and overrides class defaults.NET22
Compute network=address AND mask. Host bits zero identify the block start; host bits one give broadcast. With 172.16.28.252/20, the third octet is grouped in blocks of 16, so the network is 172.16.16.0 and broadcast 172.16.31.255. A written host/prefix such as 172.105.180.0/21 need not be an aligned block label: masking yields 172.105.176.0/21.NET24

Choice by choice

A · correct — The Class A /8 default keeps first octet 10 and clears the remaining three octets.

B · incorrect — This assumes a /16 boundary instead of the explicitly invoked Class A /8 default.

C · incorrect — This assumes /24, retaining host bits that the Class A default would clear.

D · incorrect — Clearing the network octet too loses the assigned Class A network identifier 10.

  • A. Hubs operate at Layer 3; switches operate at Layer 2
  • B. Hubs send data to all connected devices; switches send data only to the intended device

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET10 · Bridges, switches and access points

NET09 · NICs, repeaters and hubs

NET-S07 · Physical signaling and legacy Ethernet cable roles

Correct answer: B — Hubs send data to all connected devices; switches send data only to the intended device

An active hub repeats incoming signals onto its other ports without examining addresses. A switch learns MAC-to-port mappings and, for the specified known unicast on another port, forwards the frame only to that destination port. Unknown unicasts and broadcasts are different cases and can be flooded. The scope restriction makes the intended contrast accurate without treating selective forwarding as a universal rule for all switch traffic.

Evidence in the complete study note

A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.NET10
A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.NET09
Ethernet switches can have fiber-optic interfaces with suitable optical transceivers. A forwarding role therefore does not impose a copper-only restriction: distinguish what the device does with frames from the physical medium used by its ports.NET-S07

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Hubs are layer-1 repeaters, not layer-3 routers; ordinary switches are layer 2.

B · correct — In this known-unicast case the hub repeats to other ports, while the switch sends only to the learned destination port.

C · incorrect — Hubs do not use IP addresses to decide forwarding; they repeat signals without address inspection.

D · incorrect — Hub versus switch is a signal-repetition versus frame-forwarding distinction; it does not impose the claimed prohibition on optical switch links.

Apply the cited definitions to the stated scope; for calculations, derive the result from the supplied prefix, bit count or resource rule.

Study-guide sections

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET17 · Transport choice, ports and connections

NET14 · Access control and reliable-link procedures

NET19 · Upper layers and the TCP/IP correspondence

Correct answer: C — Transport Layer

TCP uses sequence numbers, acknowledgments and windows to provide reliable ordered delivery between transport endpoints. Reliable link protocols can use similar mechanisms, but their scope is a single hop. The explicit end-to-end process requirement therefore selects transport. IP supplies best-effort network delivery, while session coordinates dialogs and checkpoints rather than defining TCP’s ordered-byte-stream reliability and receiver flow control.

Evidence in the complete study note

TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.NET17
Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.NET14
OSI session roles establish/manage dialogs and can coordinate checkpoints so transfer resumes after interruption. Presentation roles translate encodings and handle compression/encryption. Compression reduces representation size; encryption hides content and need not shrink it. Application protocols provide services directly to applications. Practical implementations distribute these functions differently; TLS is not proof of a separate physical presentation-layer device.NET19

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — IP is best effort and does not supply the listed reliable acknowledgment/retransmission service.

B · incorrect — Data-link reliability is hop-local rather than the required end-to-end process service.

C · correct — Transport supplies TCP’s end-to-end sequencing, acknowledgments and receiver flow control.

D · incorrect — Session manages dialogs/checkpoints rather than the specifically listed link/TCP reliability machinery.

Question 272

For the IP address 192.168.2.64/26, what is the broadcast address?

  • A. 192.168.2.65
  • B. 192.168.2.126
  • C. 192.168.2.127
  • D. 192.168.2.255

Source

  • Data Communication & Networking review questions · Question 48

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Apply the cited definitions to the stated scope; for calculations, derive the result from the supplied prefix, bit count or resource rule.

Study-guide sections

NET25 · Find subnet bounds and usable hosts

NET24 · Masks, prefixes and binary AND

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET25 · Find subnet bounds and usable hosts

NET24 · Masks, prefixes and binary AND

Correct answer: C — 192.168.2.127

A /26 has blocks of 64 addresses. Starting at .64, this block runs through .127; the final address has all six host bits one and is broadcast. .65 and .126 are ordinary first/last hosts. .255 belongs to another /26 block, so it is not this subnet’s broadcast.

Evidence in the complete study note

192.168.2.64/26 spans .64–.127; usable .65–.126 gives 62 hosts. 192.168.10.25/28 spans .16–.31, so its network is .16. 172.17.128.0/21 spans 172.17.128.0–172.17.135.255; .128.255 and .135.0 are valid interior hosts, but .135.255 is broadcast. /27 gives 32 total and 30 usable, not 32 usable.NET25
Compute network=address AND mask. Host bits zero identify the block start; host bits one give broadcast. With 172.16.28.252/20, the third octet is grouped in blocks of 16, so the network is 172.16.16.0 and broadcast 172.16.31.255. A written host/prefix such as 172.105.180.0/21 need not be an aligned block label: masking yields 172.105.176.0/21.NET24

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — 192.168.2.65 is the first usable host, not the all-host-bits-one address.

B · incorrect — 192.168.2.126 is the last usable host, one address below broadcast.

C · correct — The .64–.127 /26 block ends at .127, its directed broadcast.

D · incorrect — The .255 address is outside this .64–.127 subnet block.

Question 273

Which of the following CORRECTLY describes the role of SMTP?

  • A. Translates domain names to IP addresses
  • B. Governs how web pages are requested and delivered
  • C. Governs how email messages are sent from a client to a mail server
  • D. Enables file transfer between devices over the internet

Source

  • Data Communication & Networking review questions · Question 49

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Apply the cited definitions to the stated scope; for calculations, derive the result from the supplied prefix, bit count or resource rule.

Study-guide sections

NET21 · Web, file, mail and remote-login protocols

NET20 · DNS, DHCP and address resolution

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET21 · Web, file, mail and remote-login protocols

NET20 · DNS, DHCP and address resolution

Correct answer: C — SMTP submits and relays email

NET21 assigns SMTP mail submission and relay. A client sending a message to a mail server is therefore a correct SMTP role. DNS resolves names, HTTP serves web requests and FTP transfers files. This does not assign end-user mailbox retrieval to SMTP; POP3/IMAP serve that separate task.

Evidence in the complete study note

HTTP defines web request/response semantics; it is stateless, and a message body may be absent. HTTPS adds TLS protection. FTP transfers files using control and separate data connections; it is not the same protocol as SFTP. SMTP submits and relays mail; POP3 retrieves messages and IMAP accesses/synchronizes server mailboxes. Saying SMTP handles both sending and end-user mailbox retrieval is inaccurate.NET21
DNS resolves names to records, including IPv4 A and IPv6 AAAA addresses; it can use UDP or TCP port 53. DHCP dynamically leases IPv4 settings, commonly address, mask, gateway and DNS server. Its basic exchange is discover, offer, request, acknowledge. IP itself does not assign addresses.NET20

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — DNS resolves domain names to address records rather than SMTP.

B · incorrect — HTTP governs web requests/responses, not SMTP.

C · correct — SMTP submits mail from a client to a server and relays messages between mail servers.

D · incorrect — File transfer is the FTP service role in this comparison, not SMTP’s defining mail role.

Question 274

An omnidirectional antenna transmits signals in which pattern?

  • A. A narrow beam toward a specific target
  • B. Only vertically upward
  • C. In all directions simultaneously, creating 360-degree coverage
  • D. In a focused line-of-sight path only

Source

  • Data Communication & Networking review questions · Question 50

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Apply the cited definitions to the stated scope; for calculations, derive the result from the supplied prefix, bit count or resource rule.

Study-guide sections

NET07 · Cables, wireless and connectors

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

NET07 · Cables, wireless and connectors

Correct answer: C — 360-degree azimuth coverage, with a nonuniform vertical pattern

NET07 defines omnidirectional as broad azimuth coverage. C is correct when its 360 degrees refers to the horizontal plane, not equal power in every three-dimensional direction. Directional beams or upward-only radiation do not describe this pattern. Antenna elevation patterns can still have lobes/nulls, so the answer retains that scope qualification.

Evidence in the complete study note

Radio, microwave and infrared are unguided media. Ground waves follow Earth, sky waves can reflect from ionized layers, and line-of-sight paths require suitable visibility. Microwaves are radio waves in the broader physical classification. Infrared generally does not penetrate walls. Directionality depends on antennas: omnidirectional means broad azimuth coverage, not equal radiation in every 3-D direction. Legacy Ethernet straight-through cables join unlike MDI/MDI-X roles; crossover joins like roles, such as PC–PC or switch–switch. Auto-MDI-X can remove that requirement.NET07

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — A narrow targeted beam is directional rather than omnidirectional azimuth coverage.

B · incorrect — Upward-only radiation does not provide the broad around-the-antenna azimuth pattern.

C · correct — 360-degree azimuth coverage is the intended meaning, without asserting equal power in all three-dimensional directions.

D · incorrect — A single focused path describes a directional antenna pattern.
